t: Install A9 Voice, set it up in five short steps, then dictate your first sentence and record your first meeting note. A9 Voice is for Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit). It does two jobs. Transcribe types what you say into any app while you hold a key. Notes records a meeting, a video or a voice memo and turns it into a transcript and a summary. This page takes you from a fresh install to both.

Install Download the installer . The link always gives you the newest version. Open the file you downloaded. A9 Voice installs for your Windows user only. It does not ask for administrator rights. If Windows shows a blue Windows protected your PC screen, click More info , then Run anyway . The installer is not code-signed yet, so Windows shows this once. Later updates install quietly and do not show it. Follow the installer to the end. If A9 Voice does not open by itself, open it from the A9 Voice folder in the Start menu. A9 Voice starts with Windows and waits in the tray (the small icons by the clock). Closing its window does not quit it; the first time you close it, a notice says "A9 Voice is still running in the tray". To quit, right-click the tray icon and choose Quit .

Set up A9 Voice The first time you open A9 Voice, a setup screen walks you through five steps. A row of dots at the top shows where you are. You can click Back , Skip this step or Skip setup at any time, and you can finish later: if you close the window part-way, setup picks up where it stopped.

Step 1: your name A9 Voice asks what to call you. It fills in your Windows name. Your name labels your voice in meeting transcripts and lets summaries say "you" and mean you. Change it any time in Settings › Account . Click Continue .

Step 2: your microphone Pick your microphone, or leave Windows default . Say a few words: the bar moves when you talk and rests when you do not, and the text under it says Hearing you clearly. If nothing moves, check that the microphone is not muted. Click Continue .

h: Step 3: how A9 Voice hears you
t: Step 3: how A9 Voice hears you A9 Voice needs a speech service to turn your voice into text. Pick one; you can change it any time in Settings › Speech models (see Speech models ). On this PC is marked Recommended: free, private, works offline. Click the tile, then Download Parakeet V2 . It downloads once. Then A9 Voice checks its speed on your PC ("Checking its speed on this PC…") and the tile says Ready . After that, nothing you say leaves your PC. Parakeet V2 is an English model. Groq , Deepgram , OpenAI and ElevenLabs are cloud services. You bring your own key and pay the service directly. The setup screen notes that Groq has a free plan and that new Deepgram accounts get $200 of free credit. Custom server is for any OpenAI-compatible speech server. You add it later in Settings › Speech models . To use a cloud service, click its tile and follow the three steps shown: Click Get your free Groq key → . Your browser opens the service's own key page. Sign in there and create a key. (For Groq, this is console.groq.com/keys .) Come back to A9 Voice, click in the Paste API key box and paste the key. Click Test . A9 Voice saves the key and tries it. A line says Connected and shows what it heard. The tile then says Key saved . The key is stored in Windows Credential Manager, never in a file. The first service that has a key becomes the one A9 Voice uses. You can pick nothing and click Continue anyway; A9 Voice reminds you before your first dictation.

Step 4: try it Click in the box. Hold Ctrl + Space , say a sentence, then let go . Your words appear in the box and a line below says how long it took. While you hold the keys it says Listening… let go of the keys to finish. If something goes wrong, a card says That didn't work , explains why, and offers Try again , Pick another provider , Skip and Copy diagnostics .

Step 5: Notes The last step tells you that A9 Voice can also record meetings, and shows the record key ( Ctrl + Alt + N ). If you have no language model yet, it reminds you that summaries need one. This step is optional. Click Finish . If you want to see setup again, right-click the tray icon and choose Help › Restart setup .

Your first dictation You can dictate into any app, anywhere you can type: a document, an email, a chat, a web page. Click in a text box. Hold Ctrl + Space and talk. A small pill appears at the bottom of the screen with a level meter and a timer. It never takes focus from the app you are in. Let go. The pill says Transcribing and then Pasted , and your words appear where your cursor was. A quick tap of the key does nothing. To cancel while you are talking, press Esc . When you finish setup you land on Home , which lists your keys: Everything about dictation, including hands-free mode, is on the Transcribe page.

Your first meeting note A note is a recording of a meeting, a video or a voice memo. A9 Voice records your microphone and the sound your PC plays, so it hears both sides of a call. No bot joins the meeting.

h: 1. Check which models it will use
t: 1. Check which models it will use The three chips at the top right show what A9 Voice uses: Dictation (speech to text for dictating), Notes (speech to text for meetings) and AI (the language model that writes summaries and answers questions). Click a chip to switch. Notes can use Deepgram, ElevenLabs, a model on this PC, or the other services you have set up. Deepgram, ElevenLabs and models on this PC tell the people on a call apart. The others label lines Me and Them. If you only added a Groq key, open the Notes chip and pick it. AI needs a key from a language-model service. Without one, you still get a transcript, but no summary. Add one in Settings › Language models (see Language models ).

2. Start recording Open Notes and click Record , or press Ctrl + Alt + N from anywhere. The Record button in the left sidebar does the same, and turns into Stop with a timer while you record. If you join a Microsoft Teams or Zoho Cliq call, A9 Voice starts by itself and shows an 8-second notice with Discard and Keep . You can turn that off, or add other meeting apps, in Settings › Recording . A small recording bar appears on your screen: It shows Recording , the time, Pause and Stop . Hover over it for more buttons: Snip (add a screenshot to the note), Live window (watch the transcript as it happens), the microphone and computer-audio pickers, and a button that shrinks it to a small pill. The full story is on Recording a meeting .

3. Stop Click the square stop button on the bar. It asks Stop recording? : choose Stop to keep the recording, or Stop & discard… to delete it (it asks once more before it deletes anything). Esc closes the question.

4. Wait for the note The note appears at once in Notes . Its row says Transcribing… and then Summarizing… . When the status disappears, the note is ready. If it says Needs a look , open it for the reason and click Try again .

5. Open it Click the note. The page has three tabs: Summary , Transcript and Ask AI . The right column lists the speakers: type a real name in a box to rename someone everywhere in the note. If the summary is missing because you had no language model, add a key, then click Regenerate summary in the right column. More on this page in The note page .

6. Export Click Export at the top of the note. Choose what to export ( Summary , Transcript or Audio recording ), pick a format (for the summary: Markdown, plain text, PDF, Word or an HTML email file), and click the blue button, for example Export Markdown . When it says Saved. , click Show in folder . Copy for email puts the summary on the clipboard, ready to paste into a new message. Every note also lives in its own folder on your PC (by default under Documents\A9 Voice\Notes ) with its summary and transcript as plain files. Open it from the ⋯ menu with Show in folder . See Templates and export for all the formats.

If something goes wrong Nothing happens when you hold the key. The sidebar shows Key in use · fix if another app has the same shortcut. Click it, or open Settings › Dictation and choose another key. The pill says a key is missing or rejected. Click the pill's Fix link, then check the key in Settings › Speech models . The note failed or has no summary. See the steps above and Troubleshooting .

Where to go next The manual is also one click away inside the app: the ? at the top right of every page opens the manual at that screen, and Manual in the sidebar (or Help › Manual in the tray menu) opens its front page. Transcribe : hands-free mode, history, Enhance with AI and what to do when text does not paste. Dictionary : teach A9 Voice your names and jargon. Speech models and Language models : choose and add services. Recording a meeting and The note page : everything about notes. Keyboard shortcuts : every key in one place. Privacy and data : where your audio, text and keys go. Updates and channels : how A9 Voice keeps itself current.

Hold a key, talk, let go, and your words are typed into whatever app you are in. Use it for emails, chats, documents and anywhere else you can type. Transcribe is A9 Voice's dictation. It needs a speech service, which you set up in Getting started or in Speech models . Everything on this page happens on your PC except the speech service you chose: your audio goes there, and nowhere else. See Privacy and data .

Dictate with the dictation key The dictation key is Ctrl + Space . Click in a text box in any app. Hold the dictation key and talk. Let go. After a moment the text appears where your cursor was. A quick tap does nothing: no sound, no pill, nothing sent. A9 Voice treats a key press as dictation only once you have held it for a moment. To change the key, open Settings › Dictation and click the Dictation key box. It says Press keys… . Press the new combination. It needs Ctrl , Alt , Shift or Win in it (F13 to F24 work alone). Press Esc to cancel. If another program already uses that key, A9 Voice tells you, and the sidebar shows Key in use · fix until you pick another. The numbers match the sections below. See Keyboard shortcuts for every key.
Cancel a dictation Press Esc while you are recording. The pill says Cancelled and nothing is sent. Esc is only watched while you record, so it works normally the rest of the time.

Hands-free mode Hands-free lets you talk for as long as you like without holding a key. Open Settings › Dictation . Hands-free mode has three choices: Choice What it does Off Only hold-to-talk. This is how a new install starts. Its own key A second key. Press it once to start, press it again to stop and insert. Its default is Ctrl + Shift + Space . Tap the dictation key A quick tap of the dictation key starts hands-free; the next tap stops it. Holding still works as hold-to-talk. With Its own key , the Hands-free key row appears. Click it to record a new key, or press Backspace while it listens to clear it. If you hold the hands-free key down for a moment and let go, it finishes like hold-to-talk. Esc cancels in every mode. Hands-free limit (1, 2, 5, 10, 15 or 30 minutes; 10 by default) stops the recording and inserts the text after that long. The pill warns you a minute before: the timer turns amber and says how long is left.

The pill While you dictate, a small pill shows what is happening. It appears at the bottom centre of the screen where the app you are working in is (you can move it to the top in Settings › General with Pill at the top of the screen ). It never takes focus, so your cursor stays where it was. It is click-through, except for its buttons. From top to bottom: Recording (red dot, level bars, timer): you are being heard. The bars move with your voice. Hands-free adds the label Hands-free · Ctrl+Shift+Space to finish (your key), a square stop button (stop and paste) and a cross (cancel). Transcribing : your speech is being turned into text. Pasted (or Typed , or Copied ) with the time it took: done. It fades after a moment. If a second service answered, it adds via Deepgram (or the one that did); if there was no internet and a model on this PC answered, it adds offline . Mic muted (in Teams or Windows) : see Microphone and muted mics . An amber message with Fix : something needs your attention, for example a missing key. Click the pill to open the setting that fixes it. Other short messages: Didn't catch that (no speech was heard), Cancelled , Nothing to paste yet , and Timed out after 15 s. Nothing was pasted , which appears if a dictation has not finished after 15 seconds. Turn on Show the pill when idle in Settings › General if you want a small dot to show that A9 Voice is running.

The Transcribe screen Click Transcribe in the sidebar to see your dictations. Each is a row with the text, the time, the app it went into and how long it took. At the top: Today , Typical speed and Words this week , counted on this PC. Type in Search dictations to find a row. Each row's buttons: Copy puts the text on the clipboard. Paste again hides A9 Voice and pastes it into the app you were in. Delete removes the row. Clear all at the bottom deletes every row, after asking. Play recording and Show in folder appear when the audio was saved (see Dictation audio ). Retry appears on a failed row. Under each text, a line says how it went in: the time, the app, and typed or copied when it was not pasted. via Groq (or the other service) means your first choice failed and the backup answered. Hover over the time on the right to see where it went: from the key release to the audio being sent, the model, and the paste. Settings › General › History kept sets how many rows stay (the last 100, 500, 1,000, 5,000 or 20,000).

Failed dictations If the speech service cannot be reached, the row says Transcription failed. The audio is saved; retry when you're back online. Click Retry and the row fills in with the text. A retry does not paste anything; use Copy to take the text. If audio saving was off, the row says The audio is gone.
Enhanced rows When Enhance with AI changed the text, the row says AI and the time it took, with Show original to see what was heard and Show enhanced to go back.

h: Copy the last transcription from the tray
t: Copy the last transcription from the tray Missed the text box? Right-click the A9 Voice icon in the tray (the small icons by the clock) and choose Copy last transcription , or open Recent and click one of your last five dictations. The text goes on your clipboard as a normal copy; paste it with Ctrl + V . Copy last transcription is greyed out while the history is empty.

Paste the last transcription again Press Alt + Shift + V (the Paste last transcription key, number 3 above) to put your newest dictation in again at the cursor. Change it in Settings › Dictation , or press Backspace while it listens to turn it off. If you have not dictated yet, the pill says Nothing to paste yet .

Microphone and muted mics A9 Voice uses the Windows default microphone, which follows what you pick in Windows. To choose one yourself, open Settings › Microphone (or Dictation microphone in Settings › Dictation ; it is the same setting). Click Test and talk: the bar should move when you talk and rest when you do not. Keep microphone ready makes dictation start a little faster. Windows shows the microphone as in use while it is on. Dictation microphone lets you use a second microphone for dictating while your headset is muted in a call. Notes can use another one: Settings › Recording › Microphone (Me) says Same as Transcribe by default. If you speak and the pill says Mic muted (in Teams or Windows) , the microphone's Windows mute switch is on (a headset can do this when you mute yourself in Teams), or the microphone is sending complete silence. A9 Voice never unmutes anything for you. Unmute, or click Use … for dictation on the pill when it offers another microphone that is not muted. Clicking the message itself opens Settings › Microphone . A microphone that is only muted inside Teams, not in Windows, still works for A9 Voice.

Sounds A soft tone plays when recording starts, stops or is cancelled, and a lower tone when something goes wrong. The start tone comes just after you press the key, so a quick tap stays silent. Turn the tones off with Sounds and set Volume in Settings › Microphone . During a call, or with a headset in call mode, the tones play on the headset's call audio and can come a moment late.

How text goes in How text goes in (number 4 above) has two choices: Paste is the default and fastest. A9 Voice puts your text on the clipboard, sends Ctrl + V , and puts back whatever you had copied before. Dictations are kept out of Windows clipboard history ( Win + V and the cloud clipboard). Type types the text key by key. Use it in apps that block paste. Related settings in the same card: Put my clipboard back afterwards (on by default), Add a space after (on by default, so the next sentence does not run on) and Language (English by default; also detect automatically, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, Japanese or Chinese). A language that is set is faster and more accurate. Click Show advanced for Paste keys (switch to Shift+Insert for some terminals and remote desktops) and Clipboard restore delay .

Dictating into A9 Voice itself You can dictate into A9 Voice's own text boxes too: Ask, a note's title, tags and transcript lines, search, and Settings. Click in the box first, then hold the dictation key. The text goes in at the cursor and the pill says Typed . If no A9 Voice text box has the cursor, the text is copied and the pill says Copied — click a text box in A9 Voice first .

Enhance with AI Enhance with AI cleans up each dictation before it is inserted. It is off by default. Open Settings › Dictation and scroll to the Enhance with AI heading. Switch Enhance with AI on. Pick a Model . If the list is empty, add a key in Settings › Language models first (see Language models ); until then text is pasted as heard. A small, fast model keeps dictation quick. Choose a Style : Light cleanup or Formal (Formal only adjusts tone a little and never adds content). Set Wait at most (1.0 to 3.0 seconds; 1.5 by default). Past this, the plain text is pasted so dictation never stalls. Optionally write Custom instructions , for example which spellings to use. They cannot override the rules below. What it does: removes "um" and "uh", fixes punctuation and capitals, and spells your Dictionary words right. What it never does: rewrite, shorten or answer what you said. If the answer comes back much longer or shorter than what you said, A9 Voice ignores it and pastes your words as heard. The History line then says AI too slow · as heard , AI failed · as heard or AI reply skipped · as heard ; when nothing needed changing it says AI: no changes . When Enhance is on, the text of each dictation is sent to the language model you chose, in addition to the speech service.

Dictation audio saved for retries By default A9 Voice keeps a small compressed copy of each dictation's audio for 7 days, so a dictation that failed can be transcribed again. Open Settings › Dictation audio . Save audio recordings turns it on or off. Audio folder shows where the files go (by default in Documents\A9 Voice\Audio , in a Transcribe folder). Change… moves it; Open shows it. Settings, history and logs stay in AppData. Keep dictation audio is 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days or Forever . Older audio is deleted daily. Audio for a failed dictation is kept until you retry or delete it.
If something goes wrong

Nothing pastes Work down this list. Nothing happens at all when you hold the key. Another program may own the shortcut. Look for Key in use · fix in the sidebar and choose another key in Settings › Dictation . Also check the tray: if you chose Pause dictation there, the keys are switched off. Hovering the tray icon says dictation paused or shows your key. The pill says "Pick how A9 Voice hears you first". No speech service is set up. Click Fix and add a key or download a model in Speech models . The pill says "key missing", "key rejected", "rate limit hit" or "timed out". Check the key in Settings › Speech models . A backup service (see Speech models ) takes over when the first one fails, and the History line shows via and its name. The pill says "No internet". The dictation is kept as a failed row if audio saving is on; click Retry on it later. If you have downloaded a model to this PC, A9 Voice uses it instead and the pill says offline . The pill says "Didn't catch that" or "Mic muted". The microphone heard nothing. Check Settings › Microphone . The pill says "Can't type into an admin window — copied instead". Windows does not let a normal app send keystrokes to a program running as administrator. Press Ctrl + V yourself; the text is on your clipboard. The pill says "Paste was blocked — copied instead" or "Typing was blocked — copied instead". Windows did not let A9 Voice send the keys. The text is on your clipboard meanwhile, so press Ctrl + V yourself. If the pill says Pasted but nothing appears, the app may ignore Ctrl + V (some terminals and remote desktops do): switch How text goes in to Type , or under Show advanced set Paste keys to Shift+Insert . The pill says "The clipboard was busy — try again". Another program was holding the clipboard. Dictate again, or use Paste again on the row. Text pasted somewhere unexpected. The text goes into the window that has focus when the transcription finishes. Keep the right window in front until the pill says Pasted . If it still does not work, see Troubleshooting .

Teach A9 Voice the names and jargon you use, and fix the words it keeps getting wrong. Use it when a name comes out misspelled every time. The Dictionary has two lists. Vocabulary is words to listen for. Always replace is a list of fixes: when A9 Voice hears one phrase, it writes another. The same lists work for dictation and for meeting notes. Click Dictionary in the sidebar. A new install starts with both lists empty.

Add vocabulary Use vocabulary for names, products and jargon: anything the speech service might otherwise spell as an ordinary word. Click Add a word or name (number 1 above) and type the word, for example a colleague's surname. Press Enter , or click somewhere else. The word becomes a chip in the list. To remove a word, click the × on its chip. Adding the same word twice, in any capitalization, does nothing the second time. Write each word the way you want it spelled.

What vocabulary does The words are sent to the speech service as hints, so it is more likely to hear and spell them correctly. Deepgram, Groq, OpenAI and custom speech servers use the hints. Deepgram takes the first 100 words in your list, so keep the ones that matter most near the start. ElevenLabs and speech models on this PC do not use the hints; use Always replace for those. The same list is also used when Enhance with AI tidies a dictation, when a meeting is transcribed, and when a meeting summary is written, which is told to spell these words as you wrote them.

Add a fix Use a fix when the same mistake keeps coming out, for example a name that is always heard as two words. Click + Add a fix (number 2 above). A new row appears. In the left box ( Heard ), type what A9 Voice writes now, for example lark spur . In the right box ( Write ), type what you want instead, for example Larkspur . Click out of the box. The fix is saved. To remove a fix, click the × at the end of its row.

How a fix matches Whole words or phrases. A fix for cat changes "cat" but not "concatenate". A phrase such as lark spur matches those words one after the other, however they are spaced. Any capitalization. lark spur , Lark Spur and LARK SPUR all match. Written exactly as you typed it on the right. If you type Larkspur , that is what appears, whatever the capitalization of what was heard. Characters such as $ are written as they are. The longest phrase wins. If you have a fix for see and another for see em dee bee , the longer one is applied first, so the phrase is not broken up. Rows with an empty Heard box are ignored. Fixes are applied to the text that comes back from the speech service, before Enhance with AI and before the text is inserted. They also apply to the transcript of a meeting note. Fixes work with every speech service, including those that do not use vocabulary hints.

h: Add a fix from a note
t: Add a fix from a note When you correct a word in a note's transcript (double-click a line, change one word, press Enter ), A9 Voice offers to apply the change everywhere. Tick Add to Dictionary and click Apply to also save the fix and the spelling here. It is not ticked unless you tick it.

Import and export The Import and Export buttons (number 3 above) share lists with a plain text file. Use them to move your Dictionary to another PC or to share it with a colleague. Windows opens its normal file window; A9 Voice cannot show that window here. Export saves a text file. It suggests the name a9voice-dictionary.txt . The message Exported. appears when it is done. Import opens a text file ( .txt ). A message says Added or updated 3 entries. (with the real number), or Nothing new in that file. Importing only adds and updates: it never deletes your existing words or fixes.

The file format One entry per line: A line with a single word or phrase is vocabulary. A line like heard => write is a fix. → works in place of => . Both sides need text. Blank lines, and lines that start with # , are skipped. An exported file looks like this: # A9 Voice dictionary # Vocabulary: one term per line Priya Larkspur # Replacements: heard => write lark spur => Larkspur ex sample ix => Examplix If a fix in the file has the same Heard phrase as one you already have, in any capitalization, its Write side is updated. Vocabulary that you already have, in any capitalization, is not added again. You can write the file by hand in Notepad. Your Dictionary is also included when you export your data from Settings › Account , which makes a zip of your settings, Dictionary, templates and tag names. API keys are never included.

If something goes wrong A word is still misspelled. If your speech service ignores hints, add a fix as well: put the misspelling in Heard and the right spelling in Write . A fix changes words you did not mean. Fixes match whole words in any capitalization, so a short phrase such as see matches every "see". Make Heard longer and more specific. The import says "Couldn't read the file". Choose a plain text file saved as .txt .

Choose what turns your voice into text, with a cloud service and your own key, a model on this PC, or (new in 0.6.0) your graphics card. A speech model is the engine that listens to audio and writes the words. A9 Voice has no engine of its own that you pay for: you bring a key for a cloud service, or you download a model that runs on your PC. You can mix them, and you can use a different one for dictation, for notes and as a spare. Everything here is in Settings › Speech models . The page has two parts: CLOUD (services you reach with a key) and ON THIS PC (models that work offline). 1: who does what. 2: the providers. 3: your own server. The line under the title shows who does what right now: Dictation , Notes and Fallback . Each name opens that model's window. Each tile also carries small badges ( Dictation , Notes , Fallback ) for what it does. A tile with a blue Add key button has no key yet; a gear means it is set up.

Choose who does what Every model's window has up to three boxes. They are how you give a model a job. Use for dictation: this model types what you say when you hold the dictation key. Use for notes: this model writes the transcript of your recordings. The box appears for every cloud provider and custom server, and for models on this PC. Use as fallback: this model steps in when the one doing dictation fails. A few rules keep you from ending up with nothing: Dictation and notes always need a model. If you uncheck Use for dictation and a fallback is set, the fallback takes over. If there is no fallback, the box stays checked and the window says Dictation needs a speech model. Pick another one first. Pick another model first, then come back. Notes work the same way: they move to the dictation model if it can do notes, otherwise the box stays checked. A model can't be its own fallback. Checking Use as fallback on the model that does dictation gives This model does dictation. The fallback has to be a different one. You can't Disconnect the model that does dictation. Choose another one for dictation first. The box stays checked and says why.

What the fallback does The fallback is tried once when the model in use fails, is rate-limited, or takes longer than the limit shown under the cloud tiles (4 s). In the pill you see via and the fallback's name when it answered. If you have a model on this PC and both cloud models fail, it answers last. With no internet at all, the cloud fallback is skipped (it would fail too) and a model on this PC answers straight away; the pill says offline . More in Without internet .

Which models tell speakers apart For notes, Deepgram and ElevenLabs (and models on this PC) tell the people on a call apart. Groq, OpenAI and custom servers can't: notes label the lines Me and Them . If you choose one of those for notes, its tile says Can't tell speakers apart: notes label lines Me / Them , and Deepgram's tile says Best at telling speakers apart . When you save your first Deepgram key and your notes model can't tell speakers apart, Use for notes starts checked for Deepgram. Your dictation model is never changed by that.

Set up a cloud provider The steps are the same for every provider. The only things that change are where you get the key and which model you pick. Your keys stay on your PC: they go into Windows Credential Manager and never into a file, a log or the app's storage. A9 Voice only ever learns "key saved" or "no key". Open Settings › Speech models and click the provider's tile. Click the big blue Get your Groq key → button (the name changes with the provider). A9 Voice opens the provider's key page in your browser. On that page, sign in, create an API key, and copy it. Come back to A9 Voice: the cursor is already in the key box. Paste the key into API key . Click Test . A9 Voice sends a 2-second test clip and shows what it heard, for example Heard “Testing one two three.” and how long it took. Nothing is saved yet. Tick the boxes for the jobs you want, then click Save . The strip under the big button follows you: Get a key , Paste it here , Test , with each one ticked when done.

Groq Key page: console.groq.com/keys . The window says Free tier, no card needed. and the button reads Get your free Groq key → . 1: the key button opens Groq's key page. Paste the key and test it. Then choose the model ( Whisper Large v3 Turbo or Whisper Large v3 ) and the jobs. 2: paste. 3: test. 4: choose jobs. 5: save. Groq can't tell speakers apart and doesn't stream. The same Groq key is also used for Language models , so you only add it once.

Deepgram Key page: console.deepgram.com . The window says $200 of free credit, no card needed. and the button reads Get your free Deepgram key → . Models: Nova-3 and Nova-2 . Deepgram tells speakers apart, which makes it the best choice for notes, and it is the one used for the live transcript during a recording (see Live window ). Once a key is saved, the key box folds away and shows Key saved and Manage key . 1: the key is saved. 2: what this model does.

OpenAI Key page: platform.openai.com/api-keys . The button reads Get your OpenAI key → , with no promise of a free tier. The model list is a drop-down. Models: GPT-4o mini Transcribe , GPT-4o Transcribe and Whisper . OpenAI can't tell speakers apart. For notes, A9 Voice uses Whisper with OpenAI because the GPT-4o models don't give the timestamps a note needs. The same key is used for OpenAI language models .
ElevenLabs Key page: elevenlabs.io/app/settings/api-keys . The button reads Get your ElevenLabs key → . Models: Scribe v2 and Scribe v1 . ElevenLabs tells speakers apart, so it works well for notes.
Providers marked Soon A few more services appear dimmed with a Soon badge. They can't be opened yet.

What the capability line means Every cloud window shows three facts under its name: Languages , Streaming and Diarization . Diarization is telling speakers apart. Streaming means the service can return words while you are still talking; the live transcript during a recording uses Deepgram, or a fast model on this PC.

Add a custom API Use Add custom API for your own server, or any service that speaks the same language as OpenAI's speech API: it must have a /audio/transcriptions address. A speech server running on your own PC or network works. Click Add custom API at the end of the cloud tiles. Fill in Name (what the tile will say), Base URL (for example http://localhost:8000/v1 ) and Model (the model name your server expects, for example whisper-small ). A9 Voice adds /audio/transcriptions to the Base URL itself. API key (optional) : fill it in only if your server needs one. Extra header (optional) and Header value : if your server wants an extra HTTP header, type its name (for example X-Org ) and its value. The value goes into Credential Manager like a key. Click Test , then tick the jobs and click Save . 1: name. 2: address. 3: model. 4: extra header. Only the Base URL is required to save. The server gets your audio, the model name, your dictation language and your Dictionary words as a hint. For notes, the server must answer with timestamps (the Whisper verbose_json style). Disconnect on a custom server removes the provider and its saved key and header.

h: Change a key or remove a provider
t: Change a key or remove a provider To replace a key: open the tile, click Manage key , paste the new one, Save . To remove one: open the tile and click Disconnect . This deletes the saved key from Credential Manager. If the provider was your fallback, the fallback is cleared. To see the keys in Windows: open Credential Manager, then Windows Credentials . A9 Voice's entries end in a slash and the provider's name (for example /groq ). Groq and OpenAI use one key for speech and for language models . Disconnecting it in either place removes it for both.

On this PC Models in the ON THIS PC part run on your computer. They are free, work offline, and nothing you say leaves the PC. They don't need a key. English-only models first, then multilingual ones. The tiles are split into ENGLISH ONLY and MULTILINGUAL : Model Languages Runs on Parakeet V2 English the processor Whisper Small, Base, Tiny (English) English the processor Parakeet V3 25 European languages, picked by the model the processor Whisper Small, Base, Tiny 99 languages the processor (Small can also use the graphics card) Whisper Medium, Large v3, Large v3 Turbo 99 languages the graphics card only The multilingual Whisper models use the language set for dictation. Parakeet V3 detects it by itself.

Download a model Click a model's tile. The window says what it is, its languages, its Size , and how much room is free: for example 111.8 GB free on this drive . Click Download . A9 Voice downloads from Hugging Face, checks every file before use, and also fetches a small set of shared tools (finding speech and telling voices apart) the first time. A progress bar shows Downloading… … of … . Click Cancel to stop. When it finishes, A9 Voice runs a quick speed test by itself. It says what it needs before you click. Cancel stops it. If the drive is too full you get Not enough free space: it needs …, and … is free ; A9 Voice keeps 500 MB spare. A download that stops, because you cancelled or the connection dropped, picks up where it stopped when you click Download again. If it ends in an error, Discard partial download clears what was fetched.
Use a model Open the model's window. The same three boxes are there: Use for dictation , Use as fallback and Use for notes . 1: speed on this PC. 2: jobs.

Speed on this PC The window shows Speed on this PC , for example 0.2 s for 3 s of speech (14× faster than speaking) . It is measured on a short built-in clip after the download. Click Test speed to measure again. Under the speed, one line tells you about live notes: Fast enough for the live transcript. The model is at least twice as fast as speech. Too slow for the live transcript on this PC; notes are transcribed after the call. The note is still recorded and gets its transcript afterwards. If notes use a model that is too slow, the live transcript stays off for that recording with the message Live transcript needs a cloud speech key or a faster PC. The note is still recorded.

Which one to pick Parakeet V2 is the app's recommendation for English, especially on a PC without a graphics card: it adds punctuation and capitals. It's the one setup offers first. Parakeet V3 if you dictate in a European language. Whisper Small, Base and Tiny : Small is more accurate, Tiny is the smallest and the least accurate. Whisper Medium, Large v3 Turbo and Large v3 are for a PC with a graphics card; see Graphics card .

Without internet With no internet, dictation and notes use a model on this PC by themselves, no clicking needed. For dictation, A9 Voice picks the best model you have downloaded for your language, in this order for English: Parakeet V2, Parakeet V3, then Whisper Small, Base and Tiny. For other languages: Parakeet V3, then Whisper Small, Base and Tiny. Models that need a graphics card are never chosen this way. The pill says offline when this happened. Notes whose cloud model can't be reached are transcribed on the PC the same way. If you have no model downloaded, dictation ends with No internet .
The models folder Models are stored in %LOCALAPPDATA%\A9 Voice\models . Click the models folder under the tiles to open it.

Delete a model Open the model's window, click Delete , then click it again to confirm. If the model is in use, the button says what uses it, for example Delete (used for dictation and notes) . Pick another model for dictation first. Deleting removes both versions of a model (processor and graphics card). The shared tools go when the last model goes.

Graphics card New in 0.6.0. A9 Voice can run the larger Whisper models on your graphics card, which is much faster than the processor on a modern graphics card. It is optional, it works with any brand of card that supports DirectX 12, and if anything goes wrong it finishes the job on the processor by itself, so you are never worse off than without it.

What uses the card Whisper Small , Medium , Large v3 Turbo and Large v3 can use the card. Medium , Large v3 Turbo and Large v3 run on the card only. Small has a processor version and a card version, so you can have either. Parakeet , voice detection and telling speakers apart always stay on the processor.

h: Turn it on and download support
t: Turn it on and download support At the top of ON THIS PC is a box with the Use graphics card switch. It is on by default. Under its name you see the card it found and its memory, written like Your card's name · 12.0 GB of memory . Below it, Graphics-card support is a small one-time download (the page shows its size: 23.9 MB). It holds the software that lets the models use your card. A9 Voice checks it when it arrives. 1: the switch. 2: the one-time download. Click Download next to Graphics-card support . A progress line shows Downloading… … of … (…%) and Cancel stops it. When it is done the line says Ready. Checked when it was downloaded. and the button becomes Remove . Remove deletes it; Download brings it back. Cancel stops the download. Remove deletes it again. You don't have to do this first. Downloading a card model downloads the support with it if it isn't there yet, and the model's window lists it: graphics-card support (23.9 MB, once) .

h: Download a model for the card
t: Download a model for the card Click a model's tile, for example Large v3 Turbo . The window says Runs on and your card's name, then It needs about 3.5 GB of graphics memory. Click Download . Support comes with it the first time. For Small (multilingual) you choose: Download for the graphics card or Download for the processor . If you already have the processor version, its window offers Faster on your card's name, the graphics-card version , with a Download button. The card version needs support. Once it is on the card, the tile reads Whisper · on followed by your card's name and carries a GPU badge. In the window, Runs says On the graphics card, offline , and the speed shown was measured on the card. Speed on this PC is measured on the card.

Choose a card If your PC has more than one card that can run models, an extra row appears: Graphics card , This PC has more than one. Models run on the one you pick. Pick one from the list; the memory is shown next to each name. Without a choice, A9 Voice uses the card Windows prefers for performance, usually the separate card rather than the integrated one. 1: pick the card to use.

Memory and the "Needs about" message A model must fit in the card's memory with some room left for Windows. If it doesn't, its window says, for example, Needs about 8.1 GB of graphics memory; this card has 4.0 GB. Try Medium instead. and the tile says Needs 8.1 GB of graphics memory with a Needs GPU badge. The model it names is the next one down in size; it may still be too big for a small card, and its own window then says so. The figures the app shows for the models that run only on the card: Model Graphics memory it needs Large v3 Turbo about 3.5 GB Medium about 4.7 GB Large v3 about 8.1 GB Whisper Small needs less than any of them. For an integrated card, the memory Windows lets it borrow from the PC counts too. Tiles say what they need. It names a model that fits.

Every state you can see What you see What it means What to do No supported graphics card found. Whisper models run on the processor. The card-only tiles say Needs a graphics card . No usable card. Use Parakeet V2 for English, as the app suggests, or a Whisper model that runs on the processor. The driver is too old for DirectX 12. Update the graphics driver. A card was found but its driver can't do the job. Update the graphics driver in Windows, then reopen the page. The switch is off and the tiles say Needs Use graphics card . The window says Turn on Use graphics card (above the models) to use this one. You turned it off. Turn Use graphics card on. Needs … of graphics memory , with a Needs GPU badge. The model is too big for the card. Choose the smaller model the message suggests. Downloading… … of … next to Graphics-card support or on a tile. A download is running. Wait, or click Cancel . Too slow for the live transcript on this PC; notes are transcribed after the call. on a model that says it runs on the card. The card is no faster than live speech, which can happen with integrated graphics. Check Speed on this PC . Use a faster model, or a cloud key for live notes. Graphics card unavailable on tiles, and The graphics card isn't working right now. Turn Use graphics card off and on to try again. The card failed (see below). Turn the switch off and on. Whisper models run on the processor. Update the graphics driver. Turn it on to use the card.

When the card fails If the card stops working in the middle of a job (it was removed, it ran out of memory, the driver crashed), A9 Voice finishes that job on the processor. You still get your text. It says Graphics card unavailable, used the processor once, in the pill and on this page. From then on the models use the processor until you turn Use graphics card off and on again, or restart A9 Voice. The row Graphics card unavailable, used the processor says The model finished on the processor. Turn Use graphics card off and on to try the card again. The job finished on the processor. The reason is kept for support. Open Settings › General and click Copy diagnostics : it includes the switch, your cards (names and memory only), the support state and the last failure.

If something goes wrong Groq key rejected , Deepgram key rejected and so on: the key is wrong or expired. Open the tile, click Manage key , paste a new one, Test , Save . … key missing : there is no saved key for that provider. Add one. … rate limit hit : you used up the provider's allowance for now. The fallback answers. … timed out or … error and a number: the provider is slow or down. The fallback answers. No internet : you are offline and no model on this PC is downloaded. Download one from ON THIS PC so dictation keeps working offline. Test works but nothing is typed: check that the model has Use for dictation ticked, in Settings › Speech models or in the Dictation chip at the top of the window. More in Troubleshooting .

Related Language models : the keys for summaries, Ask and Enhance with AI. Transcribe : dictation, which uses the model you choose here. Recording a meeting and Live window : notes use the notes model. Privacy and data : what leaves your PC and when.

Add the AI models that write your meeting summaries, answer Ask, and tidy your dictation with Enhance with AI. Use a cloud key or a model on your own PC. A language model reads text and writes text. Speech models turn your voice into words; language models do things with the words: Summaries: after a meeting, one request writes the summary, a title and tags for the note. Ask: answers your questions about one note, about the call you are in right now, or across all your notes. Enhance with AI: tidies each dictation before it is typed: removes “um” and “uh”, fixes punctuation and capitals. None of this is required. Dictation and recording work without a language model; you just don't get summaries, Ask or Enhance. Everything here is in Settings › Language models . 1: the providers, with the checkmark on the one in use. 2: tasks with their own model. 3: your own server. The checkmark on a tile is the model Enhance , Summaries and Ask all use, and the AI: chip at the top of the window shows the same one. A tile with a blue Add key button has no key yet. Under the tiles, Enhance , Summaries and Ask each have a Change link for the times you want a different model for one job; a job set that way is listed there with its own model. Enhance has its own model, so it is listed with a Change link. Everything else follows the checkmark.

Set up a provider The app offers five: OpenRouter , OpenAI , Anthropic , Groq and Google . The steps are the same for each. Your key goes into Windows Credential Manager, never into a file, a log or the app's storage. Open Settings › Language models and click the provider's tile. Click the big blue Get your OpenRouter key → button (the name changes with the provider). Your browser opens the provider's key page. There, sign in, create an API key, and copy it. Back in A9 Voice the cursor is already in the key box. Paste it into API key . Check the Model . It is a box you can type in; the list offers the provider's usual choices, and you can enter any model name the provider knows. Click Test . A9 Voice sends a short phrase full of fillers (“um so uh the release is on uh Thursday you know”) and shows the cleaned-up answer and the time, for example “So the release is on Thursday.” · 0.64 s . Nothing is saved yet. Tick Use for Enhance, summaries and Ask if this is the model for everything, then click Save . The checkmark moves to the tile and the AI: chip follows at once. 1: the key button opens OpenRouter's key page. 2: key. 3: model. 4: test. 5: use it. 6: save. The strip under the big button, Get a key , Paste it here , Test , ticks as you go.

Providers and key pages Provider Key page Models it suggests Good to know OpenRouter openrouter.ai/settings/keys Claude Haiku 4.5, Llama 3.1 8B, Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite, GPT-4.1 nano One key for models from Anthropic, Meta, Google and others. OpenAI platform.openai.com/api-keys GPT-4.1 nano, GPT-4.1 mini, GPT-4o mini Shares its key with OpenAI speech. Anthropic console.anthropic.com/settings/keys Claude Haiku 4.5 The app describes it as careful about leaving your words alone. Groq console.groq.com/keys GPT-OSS 20B, Qwen 3.8 27B, GPT-OSS 120B Open models. Shares its key with Groq speech. Google aistudio.google.com/apikey Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite, Gemini 2.5 Flash Uses Google AI Studio's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Two of the key buttons say free , because the provider's own pages say so: Get your free Groq key → ( Free tier, no card needed. ) and Get your free Google key → ( Free to use in Google AI Studio. ). The others don't promise anything. The line under the button is only there where it is true. OpenRouter is the easiest way to try several models with one key. For Enhance, pick a small, fast model; the app says a small, fast model keeps dictation quick.

A key you already added Groq and OpenAI use the same key for speech and for language models. If you set one up in Speech models , its tile here already shows the gear instead of Add key , and its window shows Key saved . Manage key replaces it. Disconnect removes it. To change a key, open the tile, click Manage key , paste the new one and Save . Disconnect deletes the saved key (for Groq and OpenAI that removes it for speech too); if that model was the one in use, Enhance and Summaries go back to nothing chosen and Automatic.
Choose which model does what Pick one model with the checkmark and it does all three jobs. You can still give one job a different model.

Enhance Ticking Use for Enhance, summaries and Ask in a model's window sets Enhance too. To give Enhance a different model, pick it under Settings › Dictation › Enhance with AI › Model . This page then lists Enhance: with that model and a Change link, and the AI: chip adds +1 override .

Summaries and titles Settings › Transcript & summary › Summary model picks the model that writes the summary, title and tags, and answers Ask. It is the model the checkmark and the AI: chip show, so changing it there moves both. Leave it on Automatic and A9 Voice uses the first one you have set up, in this order: OpenRouter (Claude Haiku 4.5), Anthropic (Claude Haiku 4.5), OpenAI (GPT-4.1 mini), Groq. Groq comes last because a long meeting can be more than a free Groq key allows per minute. Any other model you set up, including your own server, is tried after those. Automatic shows which model it would use.

Ask Ask uses the same model as summaries ( Same as summaries ). Ask your notes also has Deep answers, which read more passages; you can give those a stronger model under Settings › Search › Model for Deep answers ; this page then lists Ask (Deep answers) with it and the AI: chip adds an override.

The AI chip The AI: chip at the top of every window shows the model in use now. Click it to switch: Automatic (with the model it would pick) or one of your set-up models. This is the same pick as the checkmark: it sets Enhance, Summaries and Ask together and clears any override, and the checkmark on this page moves with it. When Enhance or Ask uses a different model, the chip says +1 override (or +2 ). Settings… opens this page. When a model recently failed or hit a limit, the chip shows an amber dot for 10 minutes. The menu says what happened and who answered instead, for example OpenRouter rate limit hit 2 min ago. Anthropic · Claude Haiku 4.5 answered instead. The amber dot means a recent problem.

When a model fails For summaries and Ask, if the chosen model is rate-limited, takes too long, or the provider has an error or rejects the key, A9 Voice tries the next model you have set up, one per provider, in the order above. You get the answer from whichever replies first. With no internet it stops, because the next one would fail the same way. So the most reliable setup is two providers with keys. Enhance is different: it uses only its own model and has a short time limit. If it can't answer in time, you get the text as heard (see below).

Enhance with AI Enhance tidies each dictation before it is typed. It is off until you turn it on, in Settings › Dictation , under Enhance with AI . Model, style, time limit and your own instructions. Enhance with AI: the switch. It removes “um” and “uh”, fixes punctuation and capitals, and spells your Dictionary words right. Model: the model that does it. Only models you have set up are listed. If none is, the row says Add a key in Settings › Language models first. Until then, text is pasted as heard. Style: Light cleanup or Formal . Formal only adjusts the tone a little: it can expand contractions and swap very casual words for neutral ones. It never adds content. Wait at most: 1.0 s , 1.5 s (the starting value), 2.0 s or 3.0 s . Past this, the raw text is pasted so dictation never stalls. Custom instructions: your own rules, for example how a name should be spelled. They can't override the rules below.

What it never does It never rewrites, shortens, reorders, summarizes, translates or answers what you said. If you dictate a question, you get the question, tidied, not an answer. What you dictated is treated as text to edit, never as instructions.

When it is skipped Dictation never fails because of Enhance. When Enhance is too slow, fails, or returns something that doesn't look like a cleanup (much longer or shorter than what you said), the text is pasted as heard. In Transcribe , the item shows AI too slow · as heard , AI failed · as heard or AI reply skipped · as heard , and a good one shows AI with the time. A link on each item switches between Show original and Show enhanced . Enhance sends the text of each dictation to the model's provider. Pick a model on your own PC if that matters; see below.

h: Use a model on your own PC
t: Use a model on your own PC Some programs run language models on your own computer and speak the OpenAI chat format, for example Ollama and LM Studio (the app itself suggests both). Add custom API connects to any of them. Start the program and make sure it is serving a model. In Settings › Language models , click Add custom API . Name: anything, for example Local model . Base URL: the server's address, as the program shows it, for example http://localhost:8000/v1 . Model: the exact model name your server has. API key (optional): leave empty unless your server wants one. Extra header (optional) and Header value: only if your server needs one; the value is stored like a key. Click Test . It stays off until Model is filled in. Then tick Use for Enhance, summaries and Ask if you want it, and Save . 1: name. 2: address. 3: model. 4: test. A9 Voice sends an ordinary chat request to your Base URL plus /chat/completions : the model name, the instructions and the text, with the key and header if you set them. Nothing else is sent, and with a server on localhost nothing leaves your PC. Your custom model also joins the Summaries order after the built-in providers. If your model is slow, remember Enhance's Wait at most limit; Test waits at least 5 seconds. Disconnect on a custom server removes it and its saved key and header.

What it costs A9 Voice doesn't charge for language models; you pay each provider directly with your own key. Settings › Usage & cost shows an estimate for the month, priced with a table of prices you can edit. See the settings reference .

If something goes wrong OpenRouter key rejected (or another name): the key is wrong or expired. Open the tile, Manage key , paste a new one, Test , Save . … key missing : add a key for that provider. … rate limit hit or … took too long : the provider is busy. Summaries and Ask move to the next model; Enhance pastes the text as heard. No internet : language models need a connection unless they run on your PC. Add your OpenRouter key in Settings › Language models to get summaries : no model is set up. Add a key for any provider above. Test is greyed out on a custom server: fill in Model . More in Troubleshooting .

Related Speech models : keys for turning speech into text. Transcribe : where Enhance with AI works. Note page : summaries, Ask and tags on a note. Search and Ask : Ask across all your notes, and Deep answers. Privacy and data : what is sent to a provider and when.

What Notes records Notes records two sides at once and keeps them apart: Microphone (Me): your side. The meeting app keeps using the microphone as before; nothing is muted or changed. Computer audio (Them): whatever your speakers or headset play, which is the other people on a call. No bot joins your meeting. A9 Voice listens on your PC. While you record, the note is already in the Notes list. When you stop, it turns into a finished note: first the transcript, then the summary. See The note page for what you get.

Start a recording by hand Use this for anything: a call A9 Voice did not notice, a video, a voice note. Open Notes and press Record . You can also press Ctrl + Alt + N anywhere, or right-click the A9 Voice tray icon and choose Start recording . The Record button, top right of Notes. The recording bar appears on your screen and the note appears at the top of the list marked Recording . The sidebar button changes to Stop with the time. If you pressed the button in the app, A9 Voice also opens the new note. While you record, the note is in the list. A note that has just been stopped shows Transcribing or Summarizing. You can change the record key in Settings › Notes › Recording ( Record key ), or clear it.

h: Let A9 Voice start it for you
t: Let A9 Voice start it for you

Choose the apps A9 Voice can start a recording by itself when a meeting app starts using your microphone. Open Settings › Notes › Recording and look at Meeting apps : Turn on the apps you use. Microsoft Teams and Zoho Cliq and Zoho Meeting are on to begin with. The others are Zoom , Webex , Slack huddles , Discord and Browser calls , and they start off. For a call in a web page (Google Meet, or Teams or Zoom on the web, in Chrome, Edge or Firefox), turn on Browser calls . Any web page that uses the microphone then counts. For any other app, use Other app . Join a call in that app first, press Choose from apps using your mic now… , then press Add next to the app. Press Remove later to forget it. Settings › Notes › Recording. Teams and Zoho Cliq are on by default. Other app lists what is using your microphone at this moment. Apps already covered above say so. Dictation never starts a recording.

How it notices a call A9 Voice reads the list Windows keeps of which apps are using the microphone (the same list behind Windows' own "microphone in use" icon). It only reads it; it never changes anything. It looks every 2 seconds. The app must hold the microphone for 5 seconds in a row before a recording starts. A short blip does not start one. The app must also be running. An app that crashed and left a stale entry does not count. Only the apps you turned on count. If two of them are in a call at once, Teams goes first. If you discard a recording, or stop one that A9 Voice started, in the middle of a call, A9 Voice will not start another one in that same call. It waits until the app lets go of the microphone.

The 8-second notice When a call starts a recording, a card appears above the bar: The notice shows which app, which template, and a countdown. Read it. It says which app it heard and which summary template it will use ( Settings › Notes › Transcript & summary › Summary template ). Press Discard within 8 seconds if this was not a call you wanted. The recording and its note are deleted. Press Keep , or do nothing. The card goes away after 8 seconds and the recording carries on.

The recording bar The bar is a small window that sits on top of your other windows. It never takes the keyboard away from the app you are in, so clicking it will not interrupt what you are typing. The bar at rest: level tile, state and time, Pause and Stop. The tile on the left moves with the sound on either side. Under Recording is the time so far, with a red dot. Pause stops recording. Press it again ( Resume ) to carry on. Paused time is silence in the recording. Stop ends the recording. It asks first (see below). Rest the mouse on the bar to show more buttons: 1 Pause, 2 Stop, 3 Snip, 4 Live window, 5 Microphone, 6 Computer audio, 7 Minimize. Snip adds a screenshot to the note. See Live window . Live window opens or closes the live transcript. See Live window . Microphone and Computer audio choose what is recorded (next section). Minimize turns the bar into a mini pill. Double-clicking the bar does the same.

h: Choose the microphone and computer audio
t: Choose the microphone and computer audio Rest the mouse on the bar and press the Microphone button (or Computer audio ). Pick one: Auto (Windows default) follows whatever Windows uses, and shows its name underneath. A device from the list. Off to stop recording that side. The last line shows the result, for example Recording from: and the device name. It says Not recording from this source when you chose Off . The list is the same for Computer audio. The change applies straight away, to this recording only. With Auto on computer audio, A9 Voice listens to every output and uses the one that is playing, so a headset that Windows switches to call mode still works. The Computer audio button only shows when the recording includes computer audio. To set the defaults for every recording, use Settings › Notes › Recording › What gets recorded : Settings › Notes › Recording, further down. Microphone (Me) is Same as Transcribe unless you pick another one. Computer audio (Them) is on or off, and Output device follows the Windows default unless you pick one. A summary template can switch computer audio off for the notes that use it ( Capture system audio in Templates and export ).

h: Move it, minimize it, bring it back
t: Move it, minimize it, bring it back Move the bar: press on its background (not on a button) and drag. Near a screen edge it snaps to that edge. It always stays fully on a screen, never under the taskbar and never lost off the edge. Where it opens: the bottom right of your main screen, just above the taskbar. A9 Voice remembers where you put it for each set of screens, so a laptop on its own and the same laptop on a dock each keep their own place. Minimize: press Minimize or double-click the bar. It becomes a mini pill : a red dot and the time. The first time, a note says Minimized here. Click to restore, or use the tray icon. The mini pill first appears at the bottom right of the screen the bar was on. Drag it to move it; it remembers its own place. A grey dot means paused. Bring it back: click the mini pill, left-click the A9 Voice tray icon, choose Show recording bar in the tray menu, or press Ctrl + Alt + B . The same key hides a full bar again. The key is Show recording bar in Settings › Notes › Recording . Start over: right-click the tray icon and choose Reset bar position . The bar goes back to the bottom right of your main screen. The mini pill: a dot and the time. Fade the minimized bar in Settings › Notes › Recording makes the mini pill fade to 60% after 5 seconds. It comes back when the mouse is on it. It is off to begin with. Paused: grey tile and the word Paused.
Stop recording

Stop, or stop and discard Press the red square on the bar. The bar asks Stop recording? Press Stop to keep the recording. A9 Voice saves it and starts the transcript. Press the x (or Esc ) to carry on recording. Stop keeps the recording. Stop & discard asks once more. To throw it away instead, press Stop & discard… . The bar asks Discard this recording? It's deleted from this PC. Press Discard to delete it, or Keep recording to carry on. Discard deletes the audio, the files and the note. The tray's Stop recording , the record key, the Stop button in the sidebar and the stop button in the Live window all stop and keep right away, without asking. After you stop, a card says Saved. Transcribing… . When the note is finished the card says Note ready, with an Open button.

h: When a recording stops by itself
t: When a recording stops by itself The call ends. When a recording belongs to a call and the app lets go of the microphone for 4 seconds, A9 Voice shows Meeting ended , Stopping in 10 s. with Stop now and Keep recording . If you do nothing it stops and keeps the recording. If the call comes back during the countdown (the microphone opens again), the countdown is cancelled. This also applies to a recording you started by hand while a call was going: it is linked to the call and ends with it. Keep recording turns it into your own recording: only you stop it (or the end of the next call). Nobody is talking. A recording you started yourself asks Still recording? after a stretch of silence on both sides. You choose how long in Settings › Notes › Recording › "Still recording?" : 5, 10, 15 (the default), 30 or 60 minutes. The card says how long is left. Press Keep recording to carry on, or Stop now . With no answer it stops and keeps the recording 2 minutes later. If someone starts talking again, the card goes away. Paused time counts as silence. Recordings that a call started do not ask; they end with the call. The card counts down. Any sound clears it. Four hours. Every recording stops after 4 hours, and the recording is kept. A recording you start by hand with no call going on is never stopped by A9 Voice except by the last two rules: silence and the four-hour limit.

h: When a call is not recorded
t: When a call is not recorded If Settings › Notes › Recording › Wait while another recording app runs is on (it is on to begin with), A9 Voice does not start by itself while another recording app is capturing the call, so two apps never record the same call. An app that is merely open, with its own recording off, does not hold A9 Voice back. When that happens the bar says so, so a missing recording is never a surprise: Press Record now to record the call anyway. Read Teams call detected: not recording and Another recording app is capturing it. Press Record now if you want A9 Voice to record it too. The message stays for 30 seconds. The Record button and the record key always work, with or without this setting.

After you stop The note stays in the Notes list and shows what it is doing: Transcribing… (with a percentage when the speech model runs on this PC), Summarizing… , or Waiting… . A note that could not be finished shows Needs a look ; open it to see why. A call that A9 Voice started is called "Teams call" (or the app's name) until the note is named. A recording you started by hand is called "Recording". When the note is ready, a card on the bar says Note ready with an Open button. The speech model that makes the transcript is chosen in Settings › Notes › Transcript & summary › Speech model . It can be a cloud service with your own key or a model on this PC; see Speech models . Telling the other people apart (Speaker 2, Speaker 3 and so on) depends on that model. Deepgram, ElevenLabs and models on this PC tell speakers apart. Other models only label lines as you and the other side. Turn Identify speakers off to stop separating them. The summary comes from the language model and template you chose; see Language models and Templates and export .

Name notes after the meeting Settings › Notes › Transcript & summary › Name notes after the meeting has three choices: On: during the first 90 seconds of a call, A9 Voice reads the title of the meeting window in Teams, Zoho Cliq or your browser and uses it as the note's name. The folder reads like "2026-10-06 Sprint Standup". Windows with no real meeting name, such as the main Teams window, are ignored. Only log what it would choose: A9 Voice does not rename anything. It records what it would have chosen in a small log file on this PC, so you can check it. Off: the AI names the note. A title you type yourself always wins. When no usable name is found, the AI names the note after the summary.

h: Record something that is not a call
t: Record something that is not a call A video, a webinar, a voice note to yourself: press Record (or Ctrl + Alt + N ) and play or speak. A video or webinar comes in on Computer audio ; your own voice comes in on Microphone . In the list the note says Computer audio , Mic only or Mic + computer audio so you can tell them apart. Turn Microphone or Computer audio to Off on the bar if you only want one side. Nothing here stops on its own except the rules above. Press Stop when you are done.

Dictating during a meeting Dictating into another app while you record does not end up in the note. While you dictate, the microphone side of the recording is silent, and the words you dictated are removed from the transcript. This is Keep dictation out of notes in Settings › Notes › Live window and it is on to begin with. Turn it off if you want everything you say in the note.

The recording badge While you record, Windows shows it outside A9 Voice's own windows: Taskbar button: a small red dot that pulses gently about once a second. While paused it is a grey pause mark. The A9 Voice icon itself never changes color. Tray icon: the usual icon with a small red dot, or a grey pause mark while paused. Hover it for A9 Voice · Recording a note. Click to show the recording bar. Click it to bring the bar back. Tray menu: Stop recording (it says Start recording when nothing records), Show recording bar , and Reset bar position . Red is only used for recording, so a red dot always means a recording is running.
Your responsibility Some places require everyone's permission before you record them. You are responsible for any consent your location requires before you record or recognize people.

If something goes wrong A call did not start a recording. Check that its app is turned on in Settings › Notes › Recording , that the app is really using the microphone (join with audio), and that the call is longer than 5 seconds. Check Wait while another recording app runs too. Press Record to start by hand. I do not see the bar. Press Ctrl + Alt + B , or left-click the tray icon, or choose Reset bar position in the tray menu. The other people are not in the note. Check that Computer audio is not Off on the bar and that the right output is chosen. Everything is labeled Me and Them. The speech model does not separate speakers. Choose another in Settings › Notes › Transcript & summary . More in Troubleshooting .

Related Live window : the transcript beside a call, and naming the people. The note page : what you get when the recording is finished. Speech models : cloud or on this PC. Keyboard shortcuts and Settings reference .

What it is The Live window sits beside your call while a note records. It is a working copy of the transcript: each person has their own color, and you can tell A9 Voice who is who as you go. When the call ends, the finished note is made from the whole recording, and the names you gave are carried into it. You do not need it. A9 Voice records without it. Use it when you want names on the note, or answers and markers during the call. For starting and stopping, see Recording a meeting . 1 Speaker strip, 2 Now, 3 Who's talking? field, 4 Live, Ask and Notes tabs, 5 Ask field. Top to bottom the window has: The Ask anything about this meeting… field. A header with what is recording ( Teams call , or Manual recording when you started it), a level meter for Me and for Them , and the time. The speaker strip : one chip per person. The transcript. Each line has a name, the time since the recording began, and the text. A grey line is not finished yet. Now (who is talking) and the Who's talking? field. The footer: the tabs Live , Ask and Notes , the markers Action , Callout and Decision , then the microphone and computer-audio pickers, Snip , pause and stop buttons, a gear and a close button. When you scroll up to read, the Live · following button changes to Jump to live . Press it to catch up.

Open it By default the window opens by itself when a recording starts, whether a call started it or you did. Otherwise: Rest the mouse on the recording bar. Press the Live window button. It stays lit while the window is open. The Live window button, shown when the mouse is on the bar. Pressing it again closes the window. The recording goes on. If the bar is minimized or hidden, a Live window button elsewhere (for example on the note page while it records) brings the bar back first, then opens the window under it. The window closes by itself when the recording stops. The × in the footer and the – in the header only hide it; the recording goes on, and the bar's button opens it again.

Where it sits Docked is the normal state. The window sits directly under the recording bar, lined up with the bar's fixed edge. Near the bottom of the screen it goes above the bar instead. It moves when you move the bar, hides when the bar becomes a mini pill, and comes back with the bar. Resize it from its edges; A9 Voice remembers that size. To put it somewhere else, drag its header (the title row). It undocks and keeps its own place and size for each screen. A button appears in the header: Dock under bar puts it back under the recording bar. Press Dock under bar in the header. Or right-click the tray icon and choose Reset bar position , which also resets the bar. Pin on top (the pin button in the header) keeps the window above other windows. It is on to begin with. The setting is remembered. The smallest size is 380 by 320 pixels. At narrow sizes the markers and pickers wrap onto a second line. At 380 pixels wide everything is still there.

h: The Live transcript needs a speech source
t: The Live transcript needs a speech source The live lines come from a live speech service, separate from the transcript of the finished note: With a Deepgram key the two sides stream to Deepgram while you record. Deepgram bills it per channel. When Notes use a model on this PC, or when you have no Deepgram key but a model on this PC is installed, the live lines are made on this PC, but only if that model keeps up with real time on your PC. With neither, the window says Live transcript needs a cloud speech key or a faster PC. The note is still recorded. Settings › Notes › Live window › Live transcript turns it off. See Speech models . If you hear the call from speakers instead of a headset, your microphone also hears them. A9 Voice does not show those repeats as lines from you.
Name the people

The speaker strip and Now The strip lists people in the order they first spoke, except that you come first once you have said something, under your own name from Settings › Account . Everyone else starts as Speaker 2 , Speaker 3 and so on. Each has a color; the first seven are different, then the colors repeat. The chip of whoever is speaking glows, and stays lit for a few seconds after they stop. Now shows only who is speaking now, for example Now: Speaker 2 , or Now: — before anyone has spoken. Under it, small and grey, after Marcus says who spoke before them. A new speaker only shows after about 1.5 seconds of continuous speech, so a short "yes" does not make it flicker. Your own chip is not clickable. It is you. With many people on the call the strip wraps and scrolls: The strip wraps; the window keeps the transcript in view.

h: Name a speaker from their chip
t: Name a speaker from their chip Click the chip of the person you want to name. The box asks Who is Speaker 2? (or Rename Speaker 2 if they already have a name). Type a name, or pick one from the list. The list has names you used in this call first, then people from your other notes (and from your saved voices, if you use Voices ). Typing narrows it down by first or last name. A name already used on this call shows whose it is. A new name appears as + Add "name" as a new person at the top. Use ↑ and ↓ to move, Enter to choose and Esc to cancel. The note page uses this same picker when you name speakers there. Press Enter or Name . The name goes on every line from that person, past and future, and into the finished note. Press Not sure to close the box without naming anyone. Names used on this call come first. A9 Voice will not let you give a speaker your own name: That's your own name. Pick the person you mean.

h: Name whoever is talking: Who's talking?
t: Name whoever is talking: Who's talking? Use this when someone is talking right now and you want to name them without hunting for their chip. Click the Who's talking? Type a name field and start typing a name. On the first letter, A9 Voice locks on to the person the window shows as talking (not you), or if nobody is, the last other person who spoke. The line above the field changes to Naming Speaker 2 (locked) . The target stays locked, even if someone else starts talking before you press Enter. Press Enter (or Tag ) to apply the name. Press Esc to cancel. If it locked on the wrong person, press change and choose who you meant. change lists the other people on the call. After a name is applied, the bar says Tagged Ana ✓ for a few seconds (the × closes it sooner; in a very short window it stays until the next change). The field goes back to Who's talking? Type a name . Tagged Ana ✓ shows in the bar for a few seconds. If nobody else has spoken yet, it says Nobody else has talked yet. Click a speaker's chip to name them.

h: Fix one line, or everything from a speaker
t: Fix one line, or everything from a speaker Sometimes the person is right but one line is wrong, or a speaker is really two people. Click the name above a line. Lines that are not finished are greyed and cannot be clicked yet. The box asks This is → . Do one of: Type a name, then press Enter or Name . Pick a person from People . Pick one of the Speakers chips to move the line to that speaker. Under Apply to , choose Just this line or Everything from that speaker. A speaker who has no name yet starts on Everything from , since you most likely mean "this is Ana". A speaker who already has a name starts on Just this line , since you are correcting one mistake. Click a name in the transcript to open it. A line named on its own shows its name with a dotted underline. Click it again to correct it. Typing the name of someone already on the call moves the line to that person. Typing your own name moves it to you. Everything from you cannot be renamed or turned into someone else; fix those lines one at a time. With Everything from and a speaker chosen, the two speakers are joined into one (see the next section).

One name, one person A name can belong to only one speaker. If you give a name that someone on the call already has, A9 Voice asks instead of deciding: The question appears above the Who's talking? field. Read Marcus is already Speaker 3. Same person? Press Merge if it is the same person. This speaker's lines, and everything they say from now on, join the other speaker, who keeps their name. Press No, different person if two people share a name. This one becomes Marcus (2) . A name made this way is never used to learn a voice. Press Esc to close the question and do nothing.

Undo Every naming action, including a merge, shows a line with what changed and an Undo button for 10 seconds. Named Speaker 4 → Dana, with Undo. Press Undo within 10 seconds. The window says Undone . Only the newest action can be undone, and the button goes after 10 seconds. An older action cannot be undone any more ( Too late to undo that one. ). Rename the person again to change it.

h: What is learned from your names
t: What is learned from your names Nothing is learned during the call. Undo leaves no trace. A name you gave to a whole speaker can teach that person's voice after the call, but only if Voices is on. A name on a single line, and a name made different like Marcus (2) , never teaches a voice.
