Every page in Settings and every option on it, in the order the app shows them, with what it does and what a new install starts with. Open Settings at the bottom of the sidebar. The list on the left has four parts: Account and General at the top, then Shared , Transcribe and Notes . In a narrow window the list turns into a drop-down called Settings page . This page follows that list. Each option is one line: its name exactly as the app shows it, what it does, and its default for a new install . A copy that was updated from an older version keeps the choices it already had. Changes save as you make them; there is no Save button except where a page says so. The Settings list. The page you pick opens on the right.

Account Account is the first page in Settings, above the groups. It holds your plan, your profile (the "You" that meetings use) and the backup of your setup. Plan: shows Preview with "all features unlocked". Every feature is on during the preview, and personal use is free. Manage license: a button that is switched off for now. Licenses arrive with 1.0. Your name: the name your own lines carry in meeting transcripts and the name summaries use for you. It is required. If you empty the box, A9 Voice goes back to your Windows account name. Setup asks for it in step 1. Other names people use: nicknames and short forms, separated by commas. Saved with your profile on this PC. Role or title: optional, saved with your profile on this PC. Organization: optional, saved with your profile on this PC. Back up or move your setup: two buttons, Import… and Export… . Export writes one zip file with your settings, your Dictionary, your summary templates (with their logos) and the names of your tags. It never contains API keys, webhook addresses, signing secrets, your history, your notes, any audio or your voiceprints. The settings in it do include folder paths, custom server addresses and your profile, so treat the file as personal. Import reads such a zip and keeps what belongs to this PC: your microphone and speaker choices, your notes folder and Audio folder, where the windows sit, whether setup is finished, your update channel and the voice-recognition switch. Your profile never leaves this PC except for your name, which goes into the instructions for summaries (see Privacy and data ).

General General has no group heading. It is the second page in Settings and it also holds the update controls and the About card, further down the same page. Start with Windows: starts A9 Voice when you sign in, waiting in the tray. On for a new install. Start minimized: no window opens at sign-in; only the tray icon. On for a new install. After an automatic update the app also comes back quietly when this is on. Show the pill when idle: keeps a small dot of the dictation pill on screen when nothing is happening. Off for a new install. Pill at the top of the screen: moves the pill from the bottom of the screen to the top. Off for a new install, so the pill sits at the bottom. History kept: how many dictations the Transcribe history keeps; older ones are deleted. Choices: Last 100, 500, 1,000, 5,000 or 20,000. Default Last 1,000. Search dictations too: lets Ctrl+K search, Ask your notes and connected AI apps include your dictation history. On for a new install. More: Transcribe and Privacy and data .

Updates The Updates card is on the General page, under the options above. The version line at the bottom of the sidebar opens it. This version: the version you run, with Check now . The line under it says what the last check found: "Checking…", "You're up to date", "Downloading" with the version, an error, or when it last checked. Channel: Stable or Dev . Stable is the default for a new install. Dev gets every new build first; Stable gets builds once they have proven reliable. Picking a channel checks for updates at once. Restart automatically when idle: when an update is downloaded and checked, restart into it after 2 minutes without dictation. Never while you are dictating or recording. If you never set it, it is off on Stable and on for Dev. Details: Updates and channels .

About The About card is at the bottom of the General page. It shows the version and the copyright line, Atlas9 LLC , and says "Proprietary, free for personal use during the preview." View license: shows the license text on the page. The link then reads Hide license . Copy diagnostics: copies a block of text to the clipboard for an email to contact@a9voice.com . It holds the version, Windows, microphone, the speech and language providers you set up (names only), your dictation shortcuts and whether they registered, the update channel, graphics-card and display details, and the last 200 log lines with anything key-like removed. It never holds API keys or transcript text. The same command is in the tray menu under Help . Open logs folder: opens the folder with the log files. Run setup again: opens the first-run setup from step 1. The tray menu does the same under Help › Restart setup ; Skip setup is there too. Third-party notices: shows the notices for the open-source parts of A9 Voice. The button then reads Hide notices . Open source on this PC: a list of the speech models you can download and the engine that runs them, each with its license. More: Troubleshooting and Privacy and data .

Speech models Part of the Shared group. Speech models turn your voice into text, for dictation and for notes. Your keys are kept in Windows Credential Manager and nowhere else. Dictation, Notes and Fallback: the line at the top names the model that handles each. Click a name to open it. Groq: cloud speech. The default for dictation, with Whisper Large v3 Turbo. You choose the model in its window. Deepgram: cloud speech with live streaming and speaker separation. The default fallback for dictation and the default for notes, with Nova-3. OpenAI: cloud speech. Its key is shared with OpenAI on the Language models page. ElevenLabs: cloud speech with speaker separation. Add custom API: adds a speech server of your own that has an OpenAI-compatible transcription endpoint, such as one running on this PC. Needs a Base URL ; give it a Name and a Model too. The API key and an Extra header are optional. API key: the key for a provider. It is saved to Windows Credential Manager when you press Save. Get your key opens the provider's own page in your browser. Test: sends a 2-second test clip to the provider and shows what it heard. Use for dictation: makes this model the one that hears you when you hold the dictation key. Default Groq. Use for notes: makes this model transcribe meetings. Default Deepgram. Models that cannot tell speakers apart label lines Me and Them. Use as fallback: the model tried once if the dictation model fails, is rate limited or takes longer than 4 seconds. Default Deepgram. It has to be a different model from the one used for dictation. Disconnect: removes the saved key (and, for a custom server, the server). It is greyed out for the model used for dictation; choose another first. Use graphics card: lets the Whisper models that support it run on a DirectX 12 graphics card. On for a new install, and it does nothing on a PC without a supported card. The line under it names the card and its memory, or says why none can be used. Integrated graphics have only memory they borrow from the PC, so the line says "shared memory" and models that need a graphics card do not run on it. Graphics card: appears only when the PC has more than one usable card. Models run on the one you pick; the best one is the default. Graphics-card support: a one-time download of about 25 MB that lets models use the card. It is checked before use. Download , Cancel and Remove manage it. Graphics card unavailable, used the processor: a notice row that appears after the card had a problem. The job finished on the processor. Turn Use graphics card off and on to try the card again. Graphics card gave a bad result, used the processor: the same kind of notice, for a card that answered with text that did not pass A9 Voice's checks. The text from the card is thrown away, the processor does the job again, and only that result is used. English only: models that run on this PC and only understand English: Parakeet V2, Whisper Small, Base and Tiny (English). Multilingual: models that run on this PC and understand many languages: Parakeet V3 and Whisper Tiny, Base and Small, plus Medium, Large v3 and Large v3 Turbo, which run on a graphics card. Model tags: a model that cannot run here says why on its tile: "Needs a graphics card", "Needs Use graphics card", "Needs" and the amount of graphics memory it wants, "Needs its own memory" (integrated graphics), or "Graphics card unavailable". The models folder: the link under the models opens the folder where they are saved, %LOCALAPPDATA%\A9 Voice\models . Without internet, dictation and notes use a downloaded model automatically. Details: Speech models .

Language models Part of the Shared group. Language models write meeting summaries and titles, answer Ask, and power Enhance with AI in Dictation. Enhance, Summaries and Ask: the lines at the top show the model each one uses, with a Change link to the page where you choose it. OpenRouter: one key for models from several companies. Your text goes to OpenRouter, which passes it to the model you picked. OpenAI: small chat models. The key is shared with OpenAI speech. Anthropic: Claude Haiku 4.5. Groq: open models on Groq. The key is shared with Groq speech. Google: Gemini models through Google AI Studio. Add custom API: adds a language-model server that has an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, for example one running on your own PC (the page gives http://localhost:11434/v1 as an example address). Needs a Base URL ; give it a Name and a Model too. The API key and an Extra header are optional. Model: the model to use at that provider. Pick from the list or type a name. Test: cleans up a short test phrase so you can see that the key works. Use for Enhance, summaries and Ask: makes this provider the one all three use, and clears any model you had set for one of them (it asks first when there is one). The checkmark on a tile marks it, and the AI: chip at the top shows it too. Disconnect: removes the saved key (or the custom server). Details: Language models .

Usage & cost Part of the Shared group. It estimates what dictation and notes cost this month from the prices below. You pay each provider directly with your own keys, and the provider's bill is the final word. Estimated this month: the total for the month, with hours of meetings and minutes of dictation. Average per meeting hour: transcript and summary cost per hour of meeting. Shows a dash until there is a meeting. Dictation this month: cost, number and minutes of dictations. By provider, this month: a bar for each provider. The table: one row per note and day with Date, Note, Providers, Length and Cost. Click a heading to sort. A row for a note opens that note. Price table (USD): opens an editable table: price per audio hour (speech), and per million tokens in and out (language models). Speech is counted per channel, so a meeting sends your side and the other side separately. Reset to defaults puts the list prices back. Connectors Part of the Shared group. Connectors let AI apps on this PC search and read your notes. It is read only, and nothing is shared until you turn it on and connect an app. Connector for AI apps: the master switch. Off for a new install. When it is off, a connected app gets a short message instead of your notes. Connect to Claude Desktop…: under Claude Desktop , a one-click connect for the one app A9 Voice can set up itself. It shows the change it will make to that app's settings file first and makes a backup copy before changing an existing file. If the connector is off, the button reads Turn on & connect to Claude Desktop… and also turns the connector on. Other apps: Copy command and Copy settings (JSON) copy what another app needs to start the connector. The app's own settings page is where you paste it. Recent requests: the log, kept on this PC, of what connected apps asked for and when. Details: Connector for AI apps .

Dictation Part of the Transcribe group. These are the keys and the way text goes into the app you are typing in. Dictation key: hold to talk, let go to insert. A quick tap does nothing. Default Ctrl + Space . Click it and press the new shortcut. If another app has it, the sidebar says Key in use · fix . Dictation microphone: the microphone for dictation. The first choice is Windows default , which follows Windows if you change it. Pick a second microphone to keep dictating while your headset is muted in a call. It is the same setting as Microphone on the Microphone page. Paste last transcription: puts the last result in again. Default Alt + Shift + V . You can clear it to turn it off. How text goes in: Paste (fastest, the default) or Type (for apps that block paste). Put my clipboard back afterwards: restores whatever you had copied once the text is in. On for a new install. Add a space after: adds a space after the text so the next sentence does not run on. On for a new install. Keep out of clipboard history: shows Always . Dictations never appear in Win+V or the cloud clipboard. Language: the language you speak. Choices: English (the default), Detect automatically, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, Japanese, Chinese. Setting it is faster and more accurate than detecting. Hands-free mode: Off (the default for a new install), Its own key (press once to start, again to stop and insert; Esc cancels) or Tap the dictation key (a quick tap starts it and the next tap stops). Hands-free key: appears with Its own key . Default Ctrl + Shift + Space . You can clear it. Hands-free limit: appears when hands-free is on. Stops and pastes after this long, with a warning a minute before. Choices: 1, 2, 5, 10, 15 or 30 minutes. Default 10 minutes. Enhance with AI: a language model tidies each dictation before it is inserted: removes "um" and "uh", fixes punctuation and capitals, and spells your Dictionary words right. It never rewrites, shortens or answers what you said. Off for a new install. The text of the dictation goes to the language model you choose. Model: the language model Enhance uses. It lists the models you have set up on Language models; until you add a key, text is inserted as heard. A small, fast model keeps dictation quick. Style: Light cleanup (the default) or Formal , which only adjusts tone a little and never adds content. Wait at most: how long Enhance may take: 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 or 3.0 seconds. Default 1.5. Past that, the raw text is inserted so dictation never stalls. Custom instructions: your own rules for Enhance, for example how to write a name. They cannot override its built-in rules. Paste keys: under Show advanced . Ctrl+V (the default) or Shift+Insert , which some terminals and remote desktops prefer. Clipboard restore delay: under Show advanced . How long the app gets to read the text before your clipboard comes back: 200, 400, 800, 1500 or 3000 ms. Default 400 ms. Details: Transcribe , Dictionary and Keyboard shortcuts .

Microphone Part of the Transcribe group. The page's own heading in the app reads Audio . Microphone: the input device for dictation. Windows default follows Windows; or pick one. Test shows a live level meter: say a few words and the bar should move when you talk and rest when you do not. Keep microphone ready: starts a little faster, because the microphone is already open. Windows shows the microphone as in use. Off for a new install. Sounds: a soft tone when recording starts, stops or is cancelled. On for a new install. In a call with a Bluetooth headset the tone plays on the headset's call audio and can come a moment late. Volume: how loud those tones are. Default is half. Details: Transcribe and Troubleshooting .

Dictation audio Part of the Transcribe group. A9 Voice can keep the audio of each dictation for a few days, so one that failed can be transcribed again. Settings, history and logs stay in the app's data folder; only audio goes in the Audio folder. Save audio recordings: keeps a small compressed file (under 100 KB a minute) for each dictation. On for a new install. Audio folder: where audio goes, Documents\A9 Voice\Audio unless you change it. Dictation audio is in its Transcribe folder and meeting audio in its Notes folder. Change… asks whether to move the existing recordings or start fresh; Open opens the folder. A9 Voice only counts, moves or deletes files it made itself. Keep dictation audio: how long audio is kept; older recordings are deleted daily. Choices: 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days or Forever. Default 7 days. Audio for a failed dictation is kept until you retry or delete it. Details: Transcribe and Privacy and data .

Recording Part of the Notes group. When a meeting app you pick uses your microphone, A9 Voice starts recording by itself, with an 8-second Discard notice. It stops when the app lets go of the microphone. Dictation never starts a recording. Microsoft Teams: the desktop app starts a recording. On for a new install. Zoho Cliq and Zoho Meeting: the desktop apps. Calls in a browser need Browser calls . On for a new install. Zoom: the desktop app. Off for a new install. Webex: the desktop app. Off for a new install. Slack huddles: the desktop app. Off for a new install. Discord: the desktop app. Off for a new install. Browser calls: Google Meet, Teams or Zoom on the web, in Chrome, Edge or Firefox. Any site using the microphone counts. Off for a new install. Other app: join a call in the app first, then pick it with Choose from apps using your mic now… . Add puts it on the list and Remove takes it off. Record key: starts and stops a recording from anywhere. Default Ctrl + Alt + N . You can clear it. Snip key: opens the snipping overlay while recording. None by default; Win+Shift+S always works too. Show recording bar: brings the recording bar back from the mini pill or the tray, or hides it. Default Ctrl + Alt + B . The tray icon does the same. "Still recording?": a recording you started yourself asks after this much silence, and stops 2 minutes later if nobody answers. Choices: 5, 10, 15, 30 or 60 minutes. Default 15. Wait while another recording app runs: A9 Voice does not start by itself while another recording app is capturing the same call, so the two never both record. The recording bar says so and offers Record now . Record always works. On for a new install. Fade the minimized bar: the mini pill fades to 60% after 5 seconds and comes back when the mouse is on it. Off for a new install. Microphone (Me): your side of the call. The default is Same as Transcribe . Shared with the meeting app; nothing is muted or changed. Computer audio (Them): records what your speakers or headset play, which is the other people in a call. On for a new install. Output device: appears when computer audio is on. Follows the Windows default unless you pick one. Details: Recording a meeting and Keyboard shortcuts .

Live window Part of the Notes group. See who said what while the meeting is still going, tag a voice with a name, mark moments and ask questions. Live transcript: shows a live transcript while you record. If Notes use a speech model on this PC that keeps up, the live transcript is made on this PC. Otherwise, with a Deepgram key saved, both sides stream to Deepgram (billed per channel). With no Deepgram key it uses a downloaded model that keeps up, and if there is none the note is still recorded without a live transcript. On for a new install. Open the Live window when a meeting starts: the window opens docked under the recording bar and moves with it. Otherwise open it from the bar's Live button. On for a new install. Keep dictation out of notes: what you dictate into other apps during a meeting is not recorded as part of it. On for a new install. Details: Live window .

Transcript & summary Part of the Notes group. These options decide how a recording becomes a transcript and a summary. Speech model: the model that transcribes notes. Default Deepgram. Deepgram, ElevenLabs and models on this PC tell speakers apart; other models label lines Me and Them. A model without a key says "(not set up)" and needs its key in Speech models first. Name notes after the meeting: uses the meeting's own name from the call app's window, so folders read like "2026-10-06 Sprint Standup". On (the default), Only log what it would choose or Off . A title you type always wins; without a usable name the AI names the note. Identify speakers: separates the other people into Speaker 2, 3 and so on. On for a new install. It needs a speech model that can do it. Summary model: the language model that writes the summary, title and tags, and answers Ask. Automatic is the default. If it hits a rate limit or takes too long, the next set-up model answers. Summary template: the sections and rules used unless a note picks another. Default Meeting Notes . Edit them in Templates. AI auto-tag: after the summary, adds up to 3 of your existing tags that clearly fit. A new tag is only ever suggested. On for a new install. Tags: the list of your tags, with how many notes use each. Rename or merge (type an existing tag's name to merge two) and Delete change every note's files. Details: Note page and Templates and export .

Templates Part of the Notes group. The page's own heading in the app reads Summary templates . A template says how the AI writes each note's summary. The starred one is the default. Default (star): the star on a template makes it the default. Default Meeting Notes . The default one cannot be deleted. Add from library: adds a copy of Meeting Recap, Stand-up, 1:1 or Decision log. + Create template: a new template with a Summary and an Action items section. Template name and Description: what the list shows. Sections: the headings of the summary, each with an instruction for what the AI writes under it. Drag to reorder, or use the arrows; the cross removes one; + Add section adds one. "Your action items" always comes first. Rules: the rules the AI follows for every section. Capture system audio: record the other people, not just your mic. On in new templates. Generate AI summary: off means transcript, title and tags only. On in new templates. Summary language: the language the summary is written in: Same as the meeting (the default), English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, Japanese or Chinese. Tags: added to every note that uses the template. Logo: Upload logo… (PNG, SVG or JPG, up to 2 MB), with an optional version for dark backgrounds. It shows on PDF, Word and email exports and on Copy for email ; the note's summary.md stays plain. Placement: Left (the default), Center or Right. Logo height: 32, 48 or 64 px at most. Default 48. Header text: a company or team name above the note. Second line: for example "Confidential: internal". Accent color: the color of headings and dividers. Use neutral clears it. Footer: a checkbox and a text, "Notes prepared with A9 Voice" by default. Off for a new template. Custom instructions: extra instructions for the AI, for example "Keep it under 200 words". View full prompt: shows the full instructions the AI will get for this template. Save, Cancel and Delete…: Save and Cancel are available once you change something. Delete… asks again before it removes a template. Details: Templates and export .

Voices Part of the Notes group. Recognize people in meetings by their voice. Voices stay on this PC. Recognize people by voice: names people on the live transcript and in the note, a few seconds after they start talking. Off until you turn it on; turning it on shows an explainer first and downloads the speaker model once. Speaker model: appears while the speaker model is not ready. Shows its download progress, or Download ( Try again after a problem). People: a list with Name, Samples, Last recognized and Meetings. Click a name for its history. Rename , Merge and Forget work on one person; Forget removes that voice from this PC for good. Not heard in 60+ days: a filter that shows voices not recognized for 60 days or more, with Forget all to remove the ones shown. Check voiceprints: lists voices that sound suspiciously alike. It never changes or deletes anything. Import voices from a file…: adds voices from a file you pick. Voices already here are left as they are. Delete all voices: removes every voice from this PC now and for good. You type DELETE to confirm. Notes keep the names they already show. Details: Voices .

Integrations Part of the Notes group. Send notes to another service when they are ready: a "second brain", an automation service or a chat channel. Your receiver gets what you tick, nothing else. Audio and voiceprints are never sent. + Add webhook: opens the form below. Each webhook then has Test , Log , Edit and Delete… . Type: Generic JSON sends the documented payload to any receiver; the other types are ready-made for automation services (JSON payload) and chat channels (the summary as text). The form explains each one. Name: how the webhook is listed. Defaults to the type's name. URL: the address to send to. It must start with https:// (an address on your own PC, such as localhost, also works). It is kept in Windows Credential Manager, like an API key. What to send: for JSON types: Summary and Action items (structured) are on for a new webhook; Decisions, Transcript, Typed notes and markers, and Image captions (never the image files) are off. Chat types always send the summary only. When: When a note finishes (the default), When a note finishes, and again when it changes (JSON types only; 60 seconds after the last change) or Manual only . Only: limit to notes with certain tags, or notes from certain templates. Empty means every note. Signing secret: optional, JSON types only. Each request then carries a signature header so the receiver can check it came from you. Header: an optional header name and value, for example Authorization . The value is kept in Windows Credential Manager. Send a test: posts a made-up note and shows the reply. Log: shows each send with its time, event, status and size, and Resend . Failed sends are retried after 10 seconds, 1 minute and 5 minutes; sends made while offline wait until you are back online, up to 24 hours. Details: Webhooks .

Storage Part of the Notes group. Each note is one folder with summary.md, transcript.md and its images, always up to date. Audio is kept separately. Notes folder: where new notes go, Documents\A9 Voice\Notes unless you change it. Change… and Open manage it. Point it at a folder your AI tools can read. Keep notes audio: how long meeting audio is kept, for checking speakers by ear. Choices: 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days or Forever. Default 30 days. Only the audio goes; summaries, transcripts and images stay until you delete the note. Audio of a note that failed or is still being written up is kept. Tidy folder names: new notes get folders named by day and meeting, like "2026-10-06 Sprint Standup". Older ones keep their names until you press Preview… , check the list and press Rename . A9 Voice only renames folders it made itself. Notes audio goes in the Notes folder inside your Audio folder (see Dictation audio). Details: Note page and Privacy and data .

Search Part of the Notes group. Search ( Ctrl+K ), Ask your notes and connected AI apps cover your A9 Voice notes. They can also cover notes that another app keeps in a folder. Also search these folders: add folders of notes or transcripts from other apps (Markdown and text files, or an exported vault). A9 Voice only reads them and never changes them. Add folder… adds one, Read again now re-reads, Remove takes one out and Make editable copies of all notes in this folder… copies a folder's notes into A9 Voice so you can regenerate summaries and fix speakers. Changes are picked up as they happen, and every folder is read again once a day. Model for Deep answers: the language model for Ask's Deep mode. Default Same as the Summary model . Deep reads many more passages than Quick and writes a dated answer with quotes; a stronger model writes better ones. Details: Search and Ask .
Plan: shows Preview with "all features unlocked". Every feature is on during the preview, and personal use is free.
Manage license: a button that is switched off for now. Licenses arrive with 1.0.

Your name: the name your own lines carry in meeting transcripts and the name summaries use for you. It is required. If you empty the box, A9 Voice goes back to your Windows account name. Setup asks for it in step 1.
Other names people use: nicknames and short forms, separated by commas. Saved with your profile on this PC.
Role or title: optional, saved with your profile on this PC.
Organization: optional, saved with your profile on this PC.

h: Back up or move your setup
t: Back up or move your setup: two buttons, Import… and Export… . Export writes one zip file with your settings, your Dictionary, your summary templates (with their logos) and the names of your tags. It never contains API keys, webhook addresses, signing secrets, your history, your notes, any audio or your voiceprints. The settings in it do include folder paths, custom server addresses and your profile, so treat the file as personal. Import reads such a zip and keeps what belongs to this PC: your microphone and speaker choices, your notes folder and Audio folder, where the windows sit, whether setup is finished, your update channel and the voice-recognition switch.
Start with Windows: starts A9 Voice when you sign in, waiting in the tray. On for a new install.
Start minimized: no window opens at sign-in; only the tray icon. On for a new install. After an automatic update the app also comes back quietly when this is on.
Show the pill when idle: keeps a small dot of the dictation pill on screen when nothing is happening. Off for a new install.

History kept: how many dictations the Transcribe history keeps; older ones are deleted. Choices: Last 100, 500, 1,000, 5,000 or 20,000. Default Last 1,000.

Connector for AI apps: the master switch. Off for a new install. When it is off, a connected app gets a short message instead of your notes.

Connect to Claude Desktop…: under Claude Desktop , a one-click connect for the one app A9 Voice can set up itself. It shows the change it will make to that app's settings file first and makes a backup copy before changing an existing file. If the connector is off, the button reads Turn on & connect to Claude Desktop… and also turns the connector on.
Other apps: Copy command and Copy settings (JSON) copy what another app needs to start the connector. The app's own settings page is where you paste it.
Recent requests: the log, kept on this PC, of what connected apps asked for and when.
Dictation key: hold to talk, let go to insert. A quick tap does nothing. Default Ctrl + Space . Click it and press the new shortcut. If another app has it, the sidebar says Key in use · fix .

Dictation microphone: the microphone for dictation. The first choice is Windows default , which follows Windows if you change it. Pick a second microphone to keep dictating while your headset is muted in a call. It is the same setting as Microphone on the Microphone page.
Paste last transcription: puts the last result in again. Default Alt + Shift + V . You can clear it to turn it off.
How text goes in: Paste (fastest, the default) or Type (for apps that block paste).
Put my clipboard back afterwards: restores whatever you had copied once the text is in. On for a new install.
Add a space after: adds a space after the text so the next sentence does not run on. On for a new install.
Keep out of clipboard history: shows Always . Dictations never appear in Win+V or the cloud clipboard.

Language: the language you speak. Choices: English (the default), Detect automatically, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, Japanese, Chinese. Setting it is faster and more accurate than detecting.
Hands-free mode: Off (the default for a new install), Its own key (press once to start, again to stop and insert; Esc cancels) or Tap the dictation key (a quick tap starts it and the next tap stops).
Hands-free key: appears with Its own key . Default Ctrl + Shift + Space . You can clear it.
Hands-free limit: appears when hands-free is on. Stops and pastes after this long, with a warning a minute before. Choices: 1, 2, 5, 10, 15 or 30 minutes. Default 10 minutes.

Enhance with AI: a language model tidies each dictation before it is inserted: removes "um" and "uh", fixes punctuation and capitals, and spells your Dictionary words right. It never rewrites, shortens or answers what you said. Off for a new install. The text of the dictation goes to the language model you choose.
Model: the language model Enhance uses. It lists the models you have set up on Language models; until you add a key, text is inserted as heard. A small, fast model keeps dictation quick.
Style: Light cleanup (the default) or Formal , which only adjusts tone a little and never adds content.
Wait at most: how long Enhance may take: 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 or 3.0 seconds. Default 1.5. Past that, the raw text is inserted so dictation never stalls.
Custom instructions: your own rules for Enhance, for example how to write a name. They cannot override its built-in rules.
Paste keys: under Show advanced . Ctrl+V (the default) or Shift+Insert , which some terminals and remote desktops prefer.
Clipboard restore delay: under Show advanced . How long the app gets to read the text before your clipboard comes back: 200, 400, 800, 1500 or 3000 ms. Default 400 ms.

Microphone: the input device for dictation. Windows default follows Windows; or pick one. Test shows a live level meter: say a few words and the bar should move when you talk and rest when you do not.
Keep microphone ready: starts a little faster, because the microphone is already open. Windows shows the microphone as in use. Off for a new install.
Sounds: a soft tone when recording starts, stops or is cancelled. On for a new install. In a call with a Bluetooth headset the tone plays on the headset's call audio and can come a moment late.
Volume: how loud those tones are. Default is half.
Save audio recordings: keeps a small compressed file (under 100 KB a minute) for each dictation. On for a new install.

Audio folder: where audio goes, Documents\A9 Voice\Audio unless you change it. Dictation audio is in its Transcribe folder and meeting audio in its Notes folder. Change… asks whether to move the existing recordings or start fresh; Open opens the folder. A9 Voice only counts, moves or deletes files it made itself.

Keep dictation audio: how long audio is kept; older recordings are deleted daily. Choices: 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days or Forever. Default 7 days. Audio for a failed dictation is kept until you retry or delete it.
Microsoft Teams: the desktop app starts a recording. On for a new install.
Zoho Cliq and Zoho Meeting: the desktop apps. Calls in a browser need Browser calls . On for a new install.
Zoom: the desktop app. Off for a new install.
Webex: the desktop app. Off for a new install.
Slack huddles: the desktop app. Off for a new install.
Discord: the desktop app. Off for a new install.
Browser calls: Google Meet, Teams or Zoom on the web, in Chrome, Edge or Firefox. Any site using the microphone counts. Off for a new install.
Other app: join a call in the app first, then pick it with Choose from apps using your mic now… . Add puts it on the list and Remove takes it off.
Record key: starts and stops a recording from anywhere. Default Ctrl + Alt + N . You can clear it.
Snip key: opens the snipping overlay while recording. None by default; Win+Shift+S always works too.
Show recording bar: brings the recording bar back from the mini pill or the tray, or hides it. Default Ctrl + Alt + B . The tray icon does the same.
"Still recording?": a recording you started yourself asks after this much silence, and stops 2 minutes later if nobody answers. Choices: 5, 10, 15, 30 or 60 minutes. Default 15.

h: Wait while another recording app runs
t: Wait while another recording app runs: A9 Voice does not start by itself while another recording app is capturing the same call, so the two never both record. The recording bar says so and offers Record now . Record always works. On for a new install.
Fade the minimized bar: the mini pill fades to 60% after 5 seconds and comes back when the mouse is on it. Off for a new install.
Microphone (Me): your side of the call. The default is Same as Transcribe . Shared with the meeting app; nothing is muted or changed.
Computer audio (Them): records what your speakers or headset play, which is the other people in a call. On for a new install.
Output device: appears when computer audio is on. Follows the Windows default unless you pick one.

Live transcript: shows a live transcript while you record. If Notes use a speech model on this PC that keeps up, the live transcript is made on this PC. Otherwise, with a Deepgram key saved, both sides stream to Deepgram (billed per channel). With no Deepgram key it uses a downloaded model that keeps up, and if there is none the note is still recorded without a live transcript. On for a new install.

h: Open the Live window when a meeting starts
t: Open the Live window when a meeting starts: the window opens docked under the recording bar and moves with it. Otherwise open it from the bar's Live button. On for a new install.
Keep dictation out of notes: what you dictate into other apps during a meeting is not recorded as part of it. On for a new install.

Speech model: the model that transcribes notes. Default Deepgram. Deepgram, ElevenLabs and models on this PC tell speakers apart; other models label lines Me and Them. A model without a key says "(not set up)" and needs its key in Speech models first.

Name notes after the meeting: uses the meeting's own name from the call app's window, so folders read like "2026-10-06 Sprint Standup". On (the default), Only log what it would choose or Off . A title you type always wins; without a usable name the AI names the note.
Identify speakers: separates the other people into Speaker 2, 3 and so on. On for a new install. It needs a speech model that can do it.
Summary model: the language model that writes the summary, title and tags, and answers Ask. Automatic is the default. If it hits a rate limit or takes too long, the next set-up model answers.
Summary template: the sections and rules used unless a note picks another. Default Meeting Notes . Edit them in Templates.
AI auto-tag: after the summary, adds up to 3 of your existing tags that clearly fit. A new tag is only ever suggested. On for a new install.
Tags: the list of your tags, with how many notes use each. Rename or merge (type an existing tag's name to merge two) and Delete change every note's files.
Default (star): the star on a template makes it the default. Default Meeting Notes . The default one cannot be deleted.
Add from library: adds a copy of Meeting Recap, Stand-up, 1:1 or Decision log.
+ Create template: a new template with a Summary and an Action items section.
Template name and Description: what the list shows.

Sections: the headings of the summary, each with an instruction for what the AI writes under it. Drag to reorder, or use the arrows; the cross removes one; + Add section adds one. "Your action items" always comes first.
Rules: the rules the AI follows for every section.
Capture system audio: record the other people, not just your mic. On in new templates.
Generate AI summary: off means transcript, title and tags only. On in new templates.
Summary language: the language the summary is written in: Same as the meeting (the default), English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, Japanese or Chinese.
Tags: added to every note that uses the template.
Logo: Upload logo… (PNG, SVG or JPG, up to 2 MB), with an optional version for dark backgrounds. It shows on PDF, Word and email exports and on Copy for email ; the note's summary.md stays plain.
Placement: Left (the default), Center or Right.
Logo height: 32, 48 or 64 px at most. Default 48.
Header text: a company or team name above the note.
Second line: for example "Confidential: internal".
Accent color: the color of headings and dividers. Use neutral clears it.
Footer: a checkbox and a text, "Notes prepared with A9 Voice" by default. Off for a new template.
Custom instructions: extra instructions for the AI, for example "Keep it under 200 words".
View full prompt: shows the full instructions the AI will get for this template.
Save, Cancel and Delete…: Save and Cancel are available once you change something. Delete… asks again before it removes a template.

Recognize people by voice: names people on the live transcript and in the note, a few seconds after they start talking. Off until you turn it on; turning it on shows an explainer first and downloads the speaker model once.
Speaker model: appears while the speaker model is not ready. Shows its download progress, or Download ( Try again after a problem).
People: a list with Name, Samples, Last recognized and Meetings. Click a name for its history. Rename , Merge and Forget work on one person; Forget removes that voice from this PC for good.
Not heard in 60+ days: a filter that shows voices not recognized for 60 days or more, with Forget all to remove the ones shown.
Check voiceprints: lists voices that sound suspiciously alike. It never changes or deletes anything.
Import voices from a file…: adds voices from a file you pick. Voices already here are left as they are.
Delete all voices: removes every voice from this PC now and for good. You type DELETE to confirm. Notes keep the names they already show.
+ Add webhook: opens the form below. Each webhook then has Test , Log , Edit and Delete… .

Type: Generic JSON sends the documented payload to any receiver; the other types are ready-made for automation services (JSON payload) and chat channels (the summary as text). The form explains each one.
Name: how the webhook is listed. Defaults to the type's name.
URL: the address to send to. It must start with https:// (an address on your own PC, such as localhost, also works). It is kept in Windows Credential Manager, like an API key.

What to send: for JSON types: Summary and Action items (structured) are on for a new webhook; Decisions, Transcript, Typed notes and markers, and Image captions (never the image files) are off. Chat types always send the summary only.
When: When a note finishes (the default), When a note finishes, and again when it changes (JSON types only; 60 seconds after the last change) or Manual only .
Only: limit to notes with certain tags, or notes from certain templates. Empty means every note.
Signing secret: optional, JSON types only. Each request then carries a signature header so the receiver can check it came from you.
Header: an optional header name and value, for example Authorization . The value is kept in Windows Credential Manager.
Send a test: posts a made-up note and shows the reply.

Log: shows each send with its time, event, status and size, and Resend . Failed sends are retried after 10 seconds, 1 minute and 5 minutes; sends made while offline wait until you are back online, up to 24 hours.
Notes folder: where new notes go, Documents\A9 Voice\Notes unless you change it. Change… and Open manage it. Point it at a folder your AI tools can read.

Keep notes audio: how long meeting audio is kept, for checking speakers by ear. Choices: 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days or Forever. Default 30 days. Only the audio goes; summaries, transcripts and images stay until you delete the note. Audio of a note that failed or is still being written up is kept.

Tidy folder names: new notes get folders named by day and meeting, like "2026-10-06 Sprint Standup". Older ones keep their names until you press Preview… , check the list and press Rename . A9 Voice only renames folders it made itself.

Also search these folders: add folders of notes or transcripts from other apps (Markdown and text files, or an exported vault). A9 Voice only reads them and never changes them. Add folder… adds one, Read again now re-reads, Remove takes one out and Make editable copies of all notes in this folder… copies a folder's notes into A9 Voice so you can regenerate summaries and fix speakers. Changes are picked up as they happen, and every folder is read again once a day.

Model for Deep answers: the language model for Ask's Deep mode. Default Same as the Summary model . Deep reads many more passages than Quick and writes a dated answer with quotes; a stronger model writes better ones.

How A9 Voice keeps itself current, the difference between Stable and Dev, and how to check for or install an update yourself. A9 Voice looks for updates in the background, downloads them, checks that they are genuine and installs them when it is safe to. You do not have to do anything, but you can check by hand, choose how early you get new builds, and decide when the app restarts.

Stable and Dev There are two channels. A channel is just a stream of builds you follow. Stable is the default for a new download. It gets a build once that build has proven reliable. Dev gets every new build first. You see new features sooner, and you may meet a rough edge before Stable does. Choose Stable unless you want to try new things early. A build reaches Stable only after it has been tried on Dev. The Changelog lists what changed in each version.

Switch channel Open Settings from the sidebar, then General . Scroll to the Updates card, to the row called Channel . Pick Stable or Dev . A9 Voice checks for updates on that channel straight away. The version line at the bottom of the sidebar also shows which channel you are on: a small Dev tag appears next to the version when you follow Dev, and nothing appears on Stable. Click the version to jump to this card.

Going back to Stable Switching from Dev to Stable does not install an older version. A9 Voice only installs a build that is newer than the one you have, so if your Dev build is ahead of Stable, nothing changes until Stable catches up. After that, updates continue as normal on Stable.

How an update reaches you A9 Voice checks for an update a few seconds after it starts and then every 6 hours while it runs. The Check for updates link in the sidebar, Check now on the Updates card and Check for updates in the tray menu check right away. The check. A9 Voice asks a9voice.com and the project's release files on GitHub, all at once, for the newest build on your channel. It takes the newest build any of them offers, and prefers a9voice.com when they offer the same one. If one place is down, the others still count. The download. The update downloads in the background while you keep working. The sidebar shows Downloading with a small progress bar. The check of the download. Every update is signed. A9 Voice checks the signature against a key built into the app before it keeps the file. If the signature does not match, the update is thrown away and you see "The update failed its signature check and was not installed". Ready. The sidebar shows Restart to update , and the Updates card shows a banner, "Update ready", with a Restart A9 Voice button. The tray menu item changes to "Update ready — Restart A9 Voice". The restart. When you press the button, A9 Voice installs and starts again. Nothing you have recorded or typed is lost. The installer runs for your Windows user only. It does not ask for administrator rights and does not show a Windows permission (UAC) prompt, and your settings, history, notes and keys stay where they are. After an update the app comes back quietly in the tray, without opening its window, when Start minimized (Settings › General) is on.

The sidebar version line The bottom of the sidebar shows your version, for example v0.6.0 , and one of these: Check for updates: press it to check now. It then says Checking… , and for a few seconds Up to date or Couldn't check . Downloading with the new version and a progress bar: an update is on its way. Restart to update: the update is ready. Press it to install now. Update after this recording: an update is ready but you are recording. Press it to queue the update; it installs when the recording and its note are finished. The button then becomes Updates after this recording , a label with nothing to press. In a narrow window the sidebar shows icons only. The version then shortens (to v0.6 ), and hovering over it or over the update button tells the rest. If pressing Restart to update fails, a short message appears under it for a few seconds, for example "Busy dictating; try again in a moment".

Restart automatically when idle On the Updates card, Restart automatically when idle decides whether A9 Voice restarts into a ready update by itself. When it is on, A9 Voice restarts into the update once you have not dictated for 2 minutes. It never does this while you are dictating, or recording, or while a note is being written up. When it is off, the update waits until you press Restart to update . If you have never touched the switch, it is off on Stable and on for Dev. Either way, an update you queued during a recording installs by itself once the recording and its note are done.

The Updates card The card is on Settings › General, under the General options and above the About card. This version shows the version you run and the last check: "Checking…", "You're up to date", "Downloading", an error message, or when it last checked ("Last checked 12 minutes ago"). Check now checks right away. Channel is the Dev / Stable choice described above. Restart automatically when idle is the switch described above. Every option is described on the Settings reference .

If something goes wrong "Couldn't reach the update server". The PC is offline or something blocks the connection. A9 Voice tries again at the next check. The update check is the only thing A9 Voice does on its own that is not part of a service you set up; see Privacy and data . "No release on the dev channel yet" (or stable). The channel has no build published yet. Switch channel or check again later. "The update failed its signature check and was not installed". The download did not match what the project signed, so A9 Voice refused it. Check again; if it keeps happening, see Troubleshooting . The version line says "Couldn't check". The check could not finish. Press Check for updates again in a minute.
Related Settings reference for the whole Updates card. Privacy and data for what the update check sends. Troubleshooting .

What leaves your PC and where it goes, how to keep everything on your PC, where your files live, how long they are kept and how to delete them. A9 Voice keeps your data on your PC. It calls speech and language services with your own keys , and only the ones you set up. There is no A9 Voice server in between, no account and no sign-in. This page lists every place data can go. Where something is a promise about how the app is built rather than a setting you can change, it says so.

The short version Audio and text go only to the services you choose , with your keys. If you use models on this PC, nothing you say leaves it. No telemetry and no analytics. A9 Voice does not report usage, crashes or anything else. This is a rule of how the app is built. Your keys live in Windows Credential Manager and nowhere else: not in settings, logs, the repository or the app's own storage. Logs hold timings, lengths and status codes, never your words or your keys. This is also a rule of how the app is built. Voiceprints stay on this PC , are opt-in, and you can delete any of them or all of them at any time. Notes are plain files in a folder you pick. Recording consent is up to you. Some places require everyone's permission to record a conversation.

h: What leaves your PC, feature by feature
t: What leaves your PC, feature by feature The table says what is sent, to whom, and what happens when you use a model on this PC instead. What you do With a cloud service With a model on this PC Dictate (hold the key) The audio of that dictation, the language, and your Dictionary words as spelling hints go to the speech service chosen for dictation. If it fails or takes longer than 4 seconds, the same audio goes once to your fallback service. Nothing leaves. Enhance with AI The dictated text, your Dictionary spellings and your custom instructions go to the one language model you chose for Enhance. Nothing leaves if that model is a server on your own PC. Live transcript during a meeting Your microphone and the computer audio stream live, as two channels, to Deepgram. If Notes use a speech model on this PC that keeps up, the live transcript is made on this PC. Meeting transcript after a recording The audio of each channel (your microphone, and what your speakers played) goes to the speech service chosen for notes. Nothing leaves. Summary, title and tags The transcript with speaker names and times, any notes you typed or marked during the meeting, your name, the template, your Dictionary spellings, your existing tags and the times and captions of your images go to a language model. Images and audio are not sent. Nothing leaves if the model is a server on your own PC. Ask (on a note, or in the Live window) The question goes to the summary model with the note's summary, its image times and captions, and its transcript (in the Live window: the transcript so far). Same as above. Ask your notes (Ctrl+K) The question and only the best matching passages (at most 10 for Quick , more for Deep ) go to the language model. Same as above. Search (Ctrl+K) Nothing. The search index is a file on your PC. Nothing. Recognize people by voice Nothing, once the speaker model is downloaded. Nothing. Export (Markdown, PDF, Word, email file, captions, audio) Nothing. Files are made on your PC. Nothing. Test button on a provider A 2-second test clip (speech) or a short test phrase (language model) goes to that provider. Nothing. Webhooks Only the parts of a note you ticked go to the address you saved. n/a The connector for AI apps Notes and action items you search for go to the AI app you connected, on this PC. What that app does with them is up to that app and its service. n/a Updates A request for the list of builds, then the update file. n/a A few details that matter: Fallback. If the service you use for dictation fails or is slow, A9 Voice sends the same audio to your fallback service. If you do not want audio to reach a second company, set Use as fallback to a model on this PC, or to none. Summaries try more than one model. Summaries, Ask and Deep answers try the model you chose first and, if it fails or is rate limited, the next language model you have set up. If you want text to go to only one place, set up only one language model. OpenRouter is a routing service: your text goes to OpenRouter, which passes it to the model you picked. The same is true of any custom server you point at a remote service. Deepgram live. With Live transcript on, a Deepgram key saved, and a Notes speech model that is not on this PC, both sides of the call stream to Deepgram live, whatever the Notes speech model is. To stop that, turn Live transcript off, use a Notes speech model on this PC, or disconnect the Deepgram key. Keeping the dictation connection ready. While A9 Voice runs and a cloud service is set for dictation, it sends that service a small request every few minutes, so the next dictation starts without delay. The request carries your key and no audio or text. With a model on this PC set for dictation, there is no such request. Dictation uses the clipboard briefly. It puts the text on the clipboard to paste it, keeps it out of Windows clipboard history and the cloud clipboard, and puts back what you had copied. When you ask for a copy yourself (tray Copy last transcription ), that copy is allowed into clipboard history.

What each service receives The services A9 Voice can call are the ones in Settings › Speech models and Settings › Language models . Each one only receives data when you set up its key (or address) and use it. Speech: Groq, Deepgram, OpenAI, ElevenLabs, and any server you add with Add custom API . Language models: OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Google, and any server you add with Add custom API . Each service's own terms say what it does with data it receives, and you pay it directly. A9 Voice has no copy of what you send.

Keeping everything on this PC You can use A9 Voice with no cloud service at all: In Settings › Speech models , download a model under On this PC (Parakeet V2 for English, or a multilingual model) and tick Use for dictation and Use for notes . Set Use as fallback to another model on this PC, or none. In the same page, Disconnect any cloud speech keys you no longer want. With no key saved, nothing can be sent there. For summaries, Enhance and Ask, run a language-model server on your own PC and add it in Settings › Language models with Add custom API . The page shows http://localhost:11434/v1 as an example address. Tick Use for Enhance, summaries and Ask (this also sets the Summary model in Settings › Transcript & summary ). Disconnect any cloud language models, because summaries fall back to them. Leave Settings › Integrations empty, and leave Connector for AI apps off if you do not want notes to reach another app. For Live transcript , use a speech model on this PC that keeps up (its window says whether it does), or turn Live transcript off. What still uses the network in this setup: The update check. A9 Voice checks a9voice.com and the project's release files on GitHub a few seconds after it starts and then every 6 hours. There is no switch to turn it off. If the PC is offline the check simply fails and tries again later. Downloads you start. Speech models come from Hugging Face. Graphics-card support (about 25 MB, once) comes from files.pythonhosted.org. The speaker model for voice recognition comes from the project's release page on GitHub. All are fixed to one version and checked against a known checksum before use. After they are downloaded you can work with no internet at all. Web pages you open. The Get your key buttons open the provider's own page in your browser. That is your browser, not A9 Voice.

No telemetry A9 Voice sends no usage data, no crash reports and no analytics. The only network calls are to the speech and language services you set up, to the update locations above, to the download locations above, and to webhook addresses you add. This is a rule of how the app is built, and the About card says it too.

Where your files live What Where Settings, history, notes database, search index, voice database %APPDATA%\com.riptide9.scribe (the folder name is the app's permanent internal identifier): settings.json , history.db , notes.db , search.db , voices.db , and window.json (the main window's size and place) Template logos %APPDATA%\com.riptide9.scribe\templates Logs %APPDATA%\com.riptide9.scribe\logs ( Open logs folder in Settings › General › About) Notes (summary, transcript, images) Documents\A9 Voice\Notes , or the folder you pick in Settings › Storage Audio (dictation and meetings) Documents\A9 Voice\Audio , or the folder you pick in Settings › Dictation audio . Dictation audio is in Transcribe , meeting audio in Notes Speech models and graphics-card support %LOCALAPPDATA%\A9 Voice\models API keys, webhook addresses and secrets Windows Credential Manager, under names that start with com.riptide9.scribe/ A copy of a recording is also kept briefly while it is being recorded and written up, in a temporary notes-spool folder in the app's data folder. It is removed afterwards. Settings, the databases and the logs stay in the app's data folder on purpose: Documents may be synced by a cloud-storage service you use, and a synced database file can be damaged. The notes and audio folders are in Documents by default, so if your Documents folder is synced, they are too. That is your choice of folder, not something A9 Voice does. If a hard crash damages the settings file or a database, A9 Voice keeps the damaged file beside the new one and tells you with a notice in the pill. Settings come back from the last good copy (or start from the defaults if there is none); a damaged history or notes database is rebuilt with the rows that could be read.

Your keys API keys are stored in Windows Credential Manager as generic credentials, on this PC. A9 Voice never writes them to settings.json , the logs, the exported settings zip or the app's own storage. The windows in the app only ever learn whether a key is set. Webhook addresses are stored the same way, because many contain a secret. Disconnect on a provider removes its key. Copy diagnostics removes anything that looks like a key before it copies the last 200 log lines.

What the logs hold The log files record timings, lengths ("90 characters"), status codes, provider and model names, and the name of the app a dictation went into. They never hold API keys or what you said. The files are kept to about 2 MB each, with a few older ones; the oldest are removed. One more file is local and worth knowing about: meeting-titles.jsonl in the logs folder. When Name notes after the meeting is on (or logging), A9 Voice reads the call app's window titles for the first 90 seconds of a call to find the meeting's name. This file keeps the titles it saw and the name it chose, for the last 200 calls, so you can check a wrong pick. It stays on your PC.

Voiceprints Recognize people by voice is off until you turn it on, after an explainer. When on, A9 Voice keeps a voiceprint for a person you tag in the Live window or name in a note: numbers that describe how they sound, not a recording. Voiceprints: are stored only in voices.db in the app's data folder, and the database is set up to overwrite deleted data; are never in your notes and never sent anywhere, including to the speech and language services, webhooks and the connector; are learned only from names you give, never from a guess; are deleted for good with Forget (one person) or Delete all voices in Settings › Voices . Turning the feature on downloads the speaker model once. See Voices .

How long things are kept What How long Dictation history The last 1,000 dictations, or the number you choose in Settings › General › History kept . Clear all in the Transcribe history deletes the rest. Dictation audio Saved by default and kept 7 days, or the time you choose in Keep dictation audio . Audio for a failed dictation is kept until you retry or delete it. Notes Until you delete the note. Notes audio 30 days, or the time you choose in Keep notes audio . Only the audio goes; the summary, transcript and images stay. Audio of a note that failed is kept. Voiceprints Until you forget them. The Voices page can show people not recognized in 60 days or more. Logs A few files of about 2 MB. Meeting-title log The last 200 calls.

Exporting and importing your setup Export… in Settings › Account writes a zip with your settings, Dictionary, templates (with logos) and tag names. It does not contain API keys, webhook addresses or secrets, your history, notes, audio or voiceprints. The settings do contain folder paths, custom server addresses and your profile, so treat the file as personal. Import… reads such a zip and keeps what belongs to this PC (devices, folders, window places, setup and update state, and the voice-recognition switch). Keys are not carried over; add them again on the new PC.

The connector and webhooks Both let something outside A9 Voice receive your notes, and both are off until you set them up. The connector for AI apps lets an AI app on this PC search and read your notes. It is read only. It can see titles, summaries, transcripts, typed notes, image captions and action items (and your dictation history if Search dictations too is on). It never gets audio, images or voiceprints. Each request is logged on the Connectors page. See Connector for AI apps . Webhooks send a note to an address you add, when it is ready. The receiver gets exactly the parts you ticked, nothing else. Audio, image files and voiceprints are never sent. Whoever can read that service can read what you send, so add only places you trust. See Webhooks .

Recording consent Some places require everyone's permission before you record a conversation. A9 Voice records what your microphone hears and what your computer plays, and no bot joins the call. Getting permission is your responsibility, not the app's.

Delete your data Pick what you want gone. Everything below is on your PC only. Dictation history: open Transcribe and use Clear all , or delete single dictations. Set Save audio recordings off in Settings › Dictation audio to stop keeping new audio. Notes: in Notes , open the ⋯ menu of a note and choose Delete… , then Delete audio, files and note . Voiceprints: Settings › Voices › Delete all voices . Keys: Disconnect on each provider in Speech models and Language models. This removes the key from Credential Manager. Webhooks: Delete… on each one in Integrations removes its address and secrets. Models: open a model under On this PC and choose Delete . Everything else: uninstall A9 Voice in Windows Settings › Apps . To also remove the files it leaves, delete the app's data folder, %APPDATA%\com.riptide9.scribe , the models folder in %LOCALAPPDATA%\A9 Voice , and your notes and audio folders in Documents\A9 Voice . Then open Windows Credential Manager , choose Windows Credentials , and remove any entries whose names start with com.riptide9.scribe/ .

Every key A9 Voice uses, what each does, its default, and where you can change it. A9 Voice has two kinds of keys. Global keys work from any app, even when A9 Voice's window is closed: dictating, recording a meeting, showing the recording bar. You can change these. Window keys work only while an A9 Voice window is in front: searching, playing a note, moving around a list. These are fixed. Keys are shown as Ctrl+Space , which means hold Ctrl and press Space .

Dictation All of these are set in Settings › Dictation . See Transcribe for what they do. Notes list Key What it does ↑ / ↓ Moves the selection up and down the list of notes. Enter Opens the selected note. F2 Renames the selected note. Then Enter saves and Esc cancels. These keys are fixed, and do nothing while you are typing in a box.

Note page Key What it does Space Plays or pauses the recording (when the note still has audio). ← / → Jumps back or forward 5 seconds. Enter In the title box, saves the new title. While you choose a key When you click one of the key boxes in Settings , it says Press keys… . Press the combination you want. Esc cancels without changing anything. Backspace or Delete clears the key, for the boxes that can be cleared. They show Not set afterwards. A key needs Ctrl , Alt , Shift or Win in it, so ordinary typing is never caught. F13 to F24 are allowed alone. Ctrl + Alt + R is reserved and cannot be chosen. Two of A9 Voice's keys cannot be the same: the second box shows Same key as and the other key's name, for example Same key as dictation or Same key as paste last transcription . If another program already uses the combination, the box shows "… is in use by another app. Quit that app or choose another key."

Other keys inside the app Enter in the Dictionary page's Add a word or name box adds the word. Esc closes the speech-model windows, the search window and the Tidy folder names window. You can also dictate into A9 Voice's own text boxes: click in the box, then hold the dictation key. See Transcribe .

If something goes wrong A key does nothing. Another program may own it. Look for Key in use · fix in the sidebar, or the message at the top of Settings › Dictation , and choose another combination. A key stopped working after you chose Pause dictation. Pause dictation in the tray menu switches the dictation keys off. Choose it again to switch them back on. Ctrl + K does not open search. The A9 Voice window must be in front, and setup must be finished. See Troubleshooting for more.
